              .access_we(access_we), .access_stb(access_stb), .access_ok(access_ok), .access_done(access_done),

              .access_skip_read(access_skip_read), .access_adr(access_adr), .access_len(access_len), 
              .access_dat_i(access_dat_i), .access_dat_o(access_dat_o));
            `endif
        end
        else begin
            `ifndef TX_ENG1_MODULE
            dspengine_8to16 #(.BASE(MAIN_SETTINGS_BASE), .BUF_SIZE(BUF_SIZE), .HEADER_OFFSET(HEADER_OFFSET)) dspengine_8to16
             (.clk(clock),.reset(reset),.clear(clear),

              .access_skip_read(access_skip_read), .access_adr(access_adr), .access_len(access_len), 
              .access_dat_i(access_dat_i), .access_dat_o(access_dat_o));

    assign debug = 0;

            access_skip_read <= (access_len == 0);
        end else begin

3. The specified amount of time should be determined by a delay parameter (delay) that you will define.

module BOR (
  input psv,
  input rst_in,
  output rst_out
);

parameter Vrst = 2.5; // reset threshold voltage
parameter delay = 10; // delay in milliseconds before reset signal de-asserts

reg rst_out_reg; // register to hold the reset signal

always @(psv) begin
  if (psv < Vrst) begin
    rst_out_reg <= 1'b1; // assert reset signal
  end else if (rst_in == 1'b1) begin
    rst_out_reg <= 1'b1; // keep reset signal asserted if rst_in is high
  end else begin
    #((delay * 1_000_000) / 2) rst_out_reg <= 1'b0; // de-assert reset signal after delay
  end
end

assign rst_out = rst_out_reg;

endmodule

module pwm (
  input clk,
  input ctrl,
  output pwm
);

  reg [7:0] duty_cycle = 8'h80; // initialize duty cycle to 50%
  reg [7:0] counter = 8'h00; // initialize counter to 0
  
  always @(posedge clk) begin
    if (counter == 8'hFF) begin
      counter <= 8'h00;
    end else begin
      counter <= counter + 1;
    end

    end else begin

  always @(posedge clk) begin

    end else begin
      duty_cycle <= ctrl;
    end
  end
  
endmodule

module j1_peripheral_interface(
    input sys_clk_i,
    input sys_rst_i,
    input miso,
    input mic_in,
    output uart_tx,
    output ledout,
    output sclk,
    output mosi,
    output ss,
    output bclk,
    output lrsel,
    inout j1_io_din,
    inout j1_io_rd,
    inout j1_io_wr,
    input [15:0] j1_io_addr,
    output [15:0] j1_io_dout
);

    // Declare wires and registers
    wire [15:0] mult_dout;
    wire [15:0] div_dout;
    wire uart_dout;
    wire [15:0] dp_ram_dout;
    wire [15:0] sd_out;
    wire [15:0] microfono_out;
    reg [4:0] cs;

    // Instantiate peripherals
    peripheral_mult mult(
        .clk(sys_clk_i),
        .rst(sys_rst_i),
        .d_in(j1_io_dout),
        .cs(cs[1]),
        .addr(j1_io_addr[3:0]),
        .rd(j1_io_rd),
        .wr(j1_io_wr),
        .d_out(mult_dout)
    );

    peripheral_div div(
        .clk(sys_clk_i),
        .rst(sys_rst_i),
        .d_in(j1_io_dout),
        .cs(cs[2]),
        .addr(j1_io_addr[3:0]),
        .rd(j1_io_rd),
        .wr(j1_io_wr),
        .d_out(div_dout)
    );

    peripheral_uart uart(
        .clk(sys_clk_i),
        .rst(sys_rst_i),
        .d_in(j1_io_dout),
        .cs(cs[3]),
        .addr(j1_io_addr[3:0]),
        .rd(j1_io_rd),
        .wr(j1_io_wr),
        .d_out(uart_dout),
        .uart_tx(uart_tx),
        .ledout(ledout)
    );

    dpRAM_interface dp_ram(
        .clk(sys_clk_i),
        .d_in(j1_io_dout),
        .cs(cs[4]),
        .addr(j1_io_addr[7:0]),
        .rd(j1_io_rd),
        .wr(j1_io_wr),
        .d_out(dp_ram_dout)
    );

    peripheral_SD sd(
        .clk(sys_clk_i),
        .reset(sys_rst_i),
        .d_in(j1_io_dout),
        .cs(cs[5]),
        .addr(j1_io_addr[3:0]),
        .rd(j1_io_rd),
        .wr(j1_io_wr),
        .d_out(sd_out),
        .sclk(sclk),
        .mosi(mosi),
        .miso(miso),
        .ss(ss)
    );

    interface_microfono microfono(
        .clk(sys_clk_i),
        .reset(sys_rst_i),
        .d_in(j1_io_dout),
        .cs(cs==5'b00011),
        .addr(j1_io_addr[3:0]),
        .rd(j1_io_rd),
        .wr(j1_io_wr),
        .d_out(microfono_out),
        .bclk(bclk),
        .lrsel(lrsel),
        .mic_in(mic_in)
    );

    // Address decoding
    always @* begin
        case (j1_io_addr[15:8])
            8'h67: cs = 5'b10000; // mult
            8'h68: cs = 5'b01000; // div
            8'h69: cs = 5'b00100; // uart
            8'h70: cs = 5'b00010; // dp_ram
            8'h71: cs = 5'b00001; // sd
            8'h72: cs = 5'b00011; // microfono
            default: cs = 5'b00000;
        endcase
    end

    // Multiplex data output
    always @* begin
        case (cs)
            5'b10000: j1_io_din = mult_dout;
            5'b01000: j1_io_din = div_dout;
            5'b00100: j1_io_din = uart_dout;
            5'b00010: j1_io_din = dp_ram_dout;
            5'b00001: j1_io_din = sd_out;
            5'b00011: j1_io_din = microfono_out;
            default: j1_io_din = 16'h0000;
        endcase
    end

    // Tri-state data output when not selected
    assign j1_io_dout = (cs == 5'b00000) ? 16'h0000 : j1_io_dout;

endmodule

module logic_function (

    input B,
    input C,
    input D,
    output reg X,
    output reg Y
);

module barrel_shifter (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input [3:0] Y,
    input [3:0] shift_amount,
    output reg [3:0] Q
);

always @(posedge clk) begin
    if (reset) begin
        Q <= 4'b0;
    end else begin
        if (shift_amount >= 0) begin
            Q <= Y << shift_amount;
        end else begin
            Q <= Y >> abs(shift_amount);
        end
    end
end

endmodule

Please act as a professional Verilog designer. Create a module that implements a finite state machine (FSM) for detecting a specific bit pattern in a 8-bit input data stream. Whenever the pattern is detected, the FSM should output a pulse of 1 clock cycle duration. The pattern to be detected is "10110101". Whenever the FSM is reset, it should start looking for the pattern from the beginning of the input data stream. Reset should be active high synchronous.
Response:
module fsm_bit_pattern_detection (
  input clk,
  input reset,
  input [7:0] data,
  output reg pulse
);

  parameter S0 = 2'b00; // Idle state
  parameter S1 = 2'b01; // First bit of pattern detected
  parameter S2 = 2'b10; // Second bit of pattern detected
  parameter S3 = 2'b11; // Pattern detected
  
  reg [1:0] state; // FSM state register
  reg [7:0] shift_reg; // Shift register for input data
  
  always @(posedge clk) begin
    if (reset) begin
      state <= S0;
      shift_reg <= 8'h00;
      pulse <= 1'b0;
    end
    else begin
      case (state)
        S0: begin // Idle state
          shift_reg <= {shift_reg[6:0], data}; // Shift in new data
          if (shift_reg == 8'b10110101) begin // Detect pattern
            state <= S3;
            pulse <= 1'b1; // Output pulse
          end
          else if (shift_reg[7] == 1'b1) begin // First bit detected
            state <= S1;
          end
        end
        S1: begin // First bit detected
          shift_reg <= {shift_reg[6:0], data}; // Shift in new data
          if (shift_reg[7:6] == 2'b10) begin // Second bit detected
            state <= S2;
          end
          else if (shift_reg[7] == 1'b0) begin // Reset if pattern not found
            state <= S0;
          end
        end
        S2: begin // Second bit detected
          shift_reg <= {shift_reg[6:0], data}; // Shift in new data
          if (shift_reg[7:5] == 3'b101) begin // Pattern detected
            state <= S3;
            pulse <= 1'b1; // Output pulse
          end
          else if (shift_reg[7:6] != 2'b10) begin // Reset if pattern not found
            state <= S0;
          end
        end
        S3: begin // Pattern detected
          shift_reg <= {shift_reg[6:0], data}; // Shift in new data
          if (shift_reg[7:0] != 8'b10110101) begin // Reset if pattern not found
            state <= S0;
          end
        end
      endcase
    end
  end

endmodule

Design a system that combines a 3-bit shift register and a 6-to-1 multiplexer. The shift register has one input port and one output port, both capable of accepting 1-bit binary numbers. The output port provides a 3-bit binary number that is the result of shifting the input value by 3 clock cycles. The system should include an additional functional module that takes in the output of the shift register and the output of the multiplexer, and outputs the logical AND of the two. The final output should be a single bit.

module my_dff ( 
    input clk, 
    input reset, 
    input d, 
    output reg q 
);

    always @(posedge clk, posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            q <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            q <= d;
        end
    end

endmodule

module shift_register_mux_and ( 
    input clk, 
    input reset, 
    input d, 
    input [2:0] sel, 
    input [3:0] data0,
    input [3:0] data1,
    input [3:0] data2,
    input [3:0] data3,
    input [3:0] data4,
    input [3:0] data5,
    output reg out 
);

    reg [2:0] shift_reg;
    wire [3:0] mux_out;
    wire [3:0] shift_out;

    my_dff dff (
        .clk(clk),
        .reset(reset),
        .d(d),
        .q(shift_reg[2])
    );

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        shift_reg <= {shift_reg[1:0], d};
    end

    assign mux_out = sel[2] ? {data0, data1, data2, data3, data4, data5} : 
                   sel[1] ? {data5, data4, data3, data2, data1, data0} :
                   sel[0] ? {data2, data3, data1, data5, data0, data4} :
                            {data0, data1, data2, data3, data4, data5};

    assign shift_out = {shift_reg[2], shift_reg[1], shift_reg[0]};

    assign out = shift_out & mux_out;

endmodule

module top_module ( 
    input clk, 
    input reset, 
    input d, 
    input [2:0] sel, 
    input [3:0] data0,
    input [3:0] data1,
    input [3:0] data2,
    input [3:0] data3,
    input [3:0] data4,
    input [3:0] data5,
    output reg out 
);

    shift_register_mux_and inst (
        .clk(clk),
        .reset(reset),
        .d(d),
        .sel(sel),
        .data0(data0),
        .data1(data1),
        .data2(data2),
        .data3(data3),
        .data4(data4),
        .data5(data5),
        .out(out)
    );

endmodule

module dual_port_ram (

    input rst_n,
    input [1:0] write_en_0,

    input [1:0] read_en_0,

    input [3:0] read_addr_1,
    output reg [15:0] read_data_1
);

- `rst`: the asynchronous reset signal (active low)
- `up_down`: the control signal that determines whether the counter should count up or down (0 for down, 1 for up)

Outputs:
- `count`: the 4-bit binary count value

You may use any Verilog constructs that you deem necessary to implement the counter.

module binary_counter(
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input up_down,
    output reg [3:0] count
);

    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst) begin
        if (!rst) begin
            count <= 4'b0000;
        end
        else if (up_down) begin
            count <= count + 1;
        end
        else begin
            count <= count - 1;
        end
    end

endmodule

module dff_2input_async_reset_set (
    input  wire clk,
    input  wire reset,
    input  wire set,
    input  wire d,
    output reg q
);

    if (reset) begin
        q <= 0;
    end else if (set) begin
        q <= 1;
    end else begin
        q <= d;
    end
end

endmodule

Implement a 4-bit shift register (right shift) with asynchronous reset, synchronous load, and enable using a combination of D flip-flops and multiplexers. The shift register should have two inputs, namely, areset and load, and two outputs, namely, q and q_next. The q_next output should be connected to the input of the next flip-flop in the shift register. The shift register should be enabled when the enable input is asserted. If both the load and enable inputs are asserted, the load input should have higher priority.
Response:
module shift_register(
    input clk,
    input areset,  // async active-high reset to zero
    input load,
    input ena,
    input [3:0] data,
    output reg [3:0] q,
    output reg [3:0] q_next);

    reg [3:0] q_temp;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge areset) begin
        if (areset) begin
            q <= 4'b0;
            q_temp <= 4'b0;
        end
        else if (ena) begin
            q <= q_next;
            q_temp <= {q[2:0], data[0]};
        end
    end

    assign q_next = (load && ena) ? data : q_temp;

endmodule

module top_module(
    input clk,
    input areset,  // async active-high reset to zero
    input load,
    input ena,
    input [3:0] data,
    output reg [3:0] q);

    wire [3:0] q_next;

    shift_register sr(
        .clk(clk),
        .areset(areset),
        .load(load),
        .ena(ena),
        .data(data),
        .q(q),
        .q_next(q_next)
    );

    always @(posedge clk or posedge areset) begin
        if (areset) begin
            q <= 4'b0;
        end
        else if (load && !ena) begin
            q <= data;
        end
        else if (ena) begin
            q <= q_next;
        end
    end

endmodule

module up_down_counter (
  input clk,
  input reset,
  input up_down,
  output reg [2:0] count
);

  always @(posedge clk) begin
    if (reset) begin
      count <= 3'b0;
    end else if (up_down) begin
      if (count == 3'b111) begin
        count <= 3'b0;
      end else begin
        count <= count + 1;
      end
    end else begin
      if (count == 3'b000) begin
        count <= 3'b111;
      end else begin
        count <= count - 1;
      end
    end
  end

endmodule

module register_adder (
  input clk,
  input rst,
  input load,
  input D,
  output reg Q
);

  always @(posedge clk or negedge rst) begin
    if (~rst) begin
      Q <= 1'b0;
    end else if (load) begin
      Q <= D;
    end else begin
      Q <= Q + D;
    end
  end

endmodule

The output of the circuit is the analog voltage (Vout).

Outputs: an analog voltage (Vout)

fs: the sampling frequency of the clock signal

You should then use this sampled value to compute the analog voltage (Vout) using the given formula.

module DAC (
  input clk,
  input [7:0] din,
  output reg Vout
);

parameter Vref = 3.3; // reference voltage of the DAC
parameter fs = 10e6; // sampling frequency of the clock signal

reg [7:0] sampled_din; // sampled value of din

always @(posedge clk) begin
  sampled_din <= din; // sample the input digital signal at the rising edge of the clock signal
  Vout <= sampled_din * Vref / 256; // compute the analog voltage using the sampled value of din
end

endmodule

Please act as a professional verilog designer. Design a module that implements a 4-bit barrel shifter. The module should have two 4-bit inputs, a and b, and a 2-bit mode input. The mode input should select one of four possible shift operations: logical left shift, logical right shift, arithmetic right shift, and rotate right. The module should have one 4-bit output, out, which is the result of the selected shift operation.
Response:
module barrel_shifter (
    input [3:0] a,
    input [3:0] b,
    input [1:0] mode,
    output reg [3:0] out
);

    always @(*) begin
        case (mode)
            2'b00: out = a << b; // logical left shift
            2'b01: out = a >> b; // logical right shift
            2'b10: out = $signed(a) >>> b; // arithmetic right shift
            2'b11: out = {a[3-b+1:0], a[3:3-b+1]}; // rotate right
        endcase
    end

endmodule

The error adapter module should be instantiated with the following parameters:
- `LATENCY_PIPELINE_STAGES`: the number of pipeline stages for the latency adapter (set to 0 for no pipeline stages)
- `IN_DATA_WIDTH`: the width of the input data bus
- `OUT_DATA_WIDTH`: the width of the output data bus

- `OUT_ERROR_WIDTH`: the width of the output error signal
- `IN_READY_LATENCY`: the number of clock cycles of latency for the input ready signal
- `OUT_READY_LATENCY`: the number of clock cycles of latency for the output ready signal

If any of these parameters are incorrect, the module should stop and display an error message.

module qsys_mm_interconnect_error_adapter (
    input clk,
    input reset_n,
    input [IN_DATA_WIDTH-1:0] in_data,
    input in_valid,
    input in_ready,
    output reg [OUT_DATA_WIDTH-1:0] out_data,
    output reg out_valid,
    output reg out_ready,
    output reg out_error
);

    // Instantiate the error adapter module with the correct parameters
    error_adapter #(
        .LATENCY_PIPELINE_STAGES(0),
        .IN_DATA_WIDTH(IN_DATA_WIDTH),
        .OUT_DATA_WIDTH(OUT_DATA_WIDTH),
        .IN_ERROR_WIDTH(1),
        .OUT_ERROR_WIDTH(1),
        .IN_READY_LATENCY(IN_READY_LATENCY),
        .OUT_READY_LATENCY(OUT_READY_LATENCY)
    ) error_adapter_inst (
        .clk(clk),
        .reset_n(reset_n),
        .in_data(in_data),
        .in_valid(in_valid),
        .in_ready(in_ready),
        .out_data(out_data),
        .out_valid(out_valid),
        .out_ready(out_ready),
        .out_error(out_error)
    );

    // Check for the error condition
    reg [2:0] in_ready_count;
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (!reset_n) begin
            in_ready_count <= 0;
        end else begin
            if (in_valid && !in_ready) begin
                in_ready_count <= in_ready_count + 1;
            end else begin
                in_ready_count <= 0;
            end
        end
    end
    wire error_condition = (in_valid && !in_ready && (in_ready_count == 2));

    // Assert the error signal if the error condition is met
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (!reset_n) begin
            out_error <= 0;
        end else begin
            if (error_condition) begin
                out_error <= 1;
            end else begin
                out_error <= 0;
            end
        end
    end

endmodule

A Schmitt trigger is a type of digital circuit that is used to remove noise from a signal. 
The circuit has two threshold voltages, Vt+ and Vt-, such that if the input voltage is above Vt+ the output is high, and if the input voltage is below Vt- the output is low. 
If the input voltage is between Vt+ and Vt-, the output remains in its current state.
Your module should have the following inputs and outputs:

- Vin: the input signal
- Vt+: the upper threshold voltage
- Vt-: the lower threshold voltage

Outputs: 
- Vout: the output signal

- When the input signal Vin rises above Vt+, the output signal Vout should go high.
- When the input signal Vin falls below Vt-, the output signal Vout should go low.
- If the input signal Vin is between Vt+ and Vt-, the output signal Vout should remain in its current state.
To implement the Schmitt trigger, you should use Verilog code to define the threshold voltages Vt+ and Vt- as parameters. 
You should then use these parameters to compare the input signal Vin to the threshold voltages and determine the output signal Vout.

module SchmittTrigger(
  input Vin,
  input Vt_plus,
  input Vt_minus,
  output reg Vout
);

  parameter Vt_plus = 1.2; // upper threshold voltage
  parameter Vt_minus = 0.8; // lower threshold voltage
  
  always @ (Vin, Vout) begin
    if (Vin > Vt_plus) begin
      Vout <= 1'b1;
    end else if (Vin < Vt_minus) begin
      Vout <= 1'b0;
    end
  end

endmodule

- `b_wptr`: write pointer for clock domain B
- `b_rptr`: read pointer for clock domain B

- `a_empty`: flag indicating FIFO is empty in clock domain A

- `b_empty`: flag indicating FIFO is empty in clock domain B

- `rptr_empty #(ASIZE)`: module for handling read requests
- `fifomem_dp #(DSIZE, ASIZE, FALLTHROUGH)`: module for the FIFO RAM

module fifo_ram (
  input a_clk,
  input [DSIZE-1:0] a_wdata,
  output [DSIZE-1:0] a_rdata,
  input [ASIZE-1:0] a_addr,
  input a_rinc,
  input a_winc,
  input a_dir,

  input b_clk,
  input [DSIZE-1:0] b_wdata,
  output [DSIZE-1:0] b_rdata,
  input [ASIZE-1:0] b_addr,
  input b_rinc,
  input b_winc,
  input b_dir,

  output [ASIZE-1:0] a2b_wptr,
  output [ASIZE-1:0] a2b_rptr,
  output [ASIZE-1:0] b_wptr,
  output [ASIZE-1:0] b_rptr,
  output a_afull,
  output a_empty,
  output b_afull,
  output b_empty
);

  // Outputs valid when dir == 0 (b is writing)
  wptr_full #(ASIZE) b_wptr_inst (
    .wclk(b_clk),
    .wrst_n(b_rst_n),
    .winc(b_winc),
    .wq2_rptr(a2b_rptr),
    .awfull(b_afull),
    .wfull(b_full),
    .waddr(b_addr),
    .wptr(b_wptr)
  );

  // dir == 1 read pointer on b side calculation
  rptr_empty #(ASIZE) b_rptr_inst (
    .rclk(b_clk),
    .rrst_n(b_rst_n),
    .rinc(b_rinc),
    .rq2_wptr(a2b_wptr),
    .arempty(b_aempty),
    .rempty(b_empty),
    .raddr(b_addr),
    .rptr(b_rptr)
  );

  // FIFO RAM
  fifomem_dp #(DSIZE, ASIZE, FALLTHROUGH) fifomem_dp (
    .a_clk(a_clk),
    .a_wdata(a_wdata),
    .a_rdata(a_rdata),
    .a_addr(a_addr),
    .a_rinc(a_rinc & !a_dir),
    .a_winc(a_winc & a_dir),

    .b_clk(b_clk),
    .b_wdata(b_wdata),
    .b_rdata(b_rdata),
    .b_addr(b_addr),
    .b_rinc(b_rinc & !b_dir),
    .b_winc(b_winc & b_dir)
  );

endmodule

The `pm` output is used to control a decimal point on the display.

The `clock_1` module should count the number of seconds since the last reset and display the value on the 7-segment display. The display should show the value in decimal format, with leading zeros suppressed. For example, if the clock has been running for 5 seconds, the display should show "0005".

Assume that the slower clock signal has a frequency of 1 Hz.

module clock_1(
    input clk, // slower clock signal
    input rst, // reset signal
    input en,  // enable signal
    output [7:0] io_seg, // 7-segment LEDs on IO Shield
    output [3:0] io_sel, // Digit select on IO Shield
    output [15:0] pm // decimal point on IO Shield
);

reg [23:0] count = 0; // 24-bit counter to count seconds
reg [3:0] digit_sel = 4'b1110; // digit select counter

always @(posedge clk, posedge rst) begin
    if (rst == 1) begin
        count <= 0;
        digit_sel <= 4'b1110;
    end else if (en == 1) begin
        count <= count + 1;
        if (count == 86400) begin // 24 hours in seconds
            count <= 0;
        end
    end
end

always @(posedge clk, posedge rst) begin
    if (rst == 1) begin
        io_seg <= 8'b11111111;
        pm <= 16'b1111111111111111;
    end else if (en == 1) begin
        case (digit_sel)
            4'b1110: io_seg <= 8'b00000110; // digit 0
            4'b1101: io_seg <= 8'b01011011; // digit 1
            4'b1011: io_seg <= 8'b01001111; // digit 2
            4'b0111: io_seg <= 8'b01100110; // digit 3
            default: io_seg <= 8'b11111111; // turn off all segments
        endcase
        
        if (count < 10) begin
            io_seg[3:0] = 4'b0000; // suppress leading zeros
        end else if (count < 100) begin
            io_seg[7:4] = 4'b0000; // suppress leading zeros
        end else if (count < 1000) begin
            io_seg[7:4] = 4'b0000; // suppress leading zeros
            io_seg[3:0] = count[9:6];
        end else if (count < 10000) begin
            io_seg[7:4] = 4'b0000; // suppress leading zeros
            io_seg[3:0] = count[13:10];
            digit_sel <= 4'b1101; // select digit 1
        end else if (count < 100000) begin
            io_seg[7:4] = count[19:16];
            io_seg[3:0] = count[13:10];
            digit_sel <= 4'b1011; // select digit 2
        end else if (count < 1000000) begin
            io_seg[7:4] = count[19:16];
            io_seg[3:0] = count[23:20];
            digit_sel <= 4'b0111; // select digit 3
        end else begin
            io_seg <= 8'b11111111; // turn off all segments
        end
        
        pm <= 16'b1111111111111110; // turn off decimal point
    end
end

always @(posedge clk, posedge rst) begin
    if (rst == 1) begin
        io_sel <= 4'b1110; // select digit 0
    end else if (en == 1) begin
        case (digit_sel)
            4'b1110: io_sel <= 4'b1101; // select digit 1
            4'b1101: io_sel <= 4'b1011; // select digit 2
            4'b1011: io_sel <= 4'b0111; // select digit 3
            4'b0111: io_sel <= 4'b1110; // select digit 0
            default: io_sel <= 4'b1110; // select digit 0
        endcase
    end
end

endmodule

You are tasked with designing a Verilog module for integer division. The module should take in two 8-bit inputs, `div` and `dvr`, representing the dividend and divisor respectively, as well as a clock signal `clk`. The module should output two 8-bit values, `quotient` and `remainder`, representing the result of the division. 

Your task is to implement the `divider` module, which should perform integer division using the following algorithm:
- Initialize the remainder (`rem`) to zero and the quotient (`qu`) to the dividend (`div`).
- For each bit of the dividend (starting from the most significant bit):
  - Shift the remainder and quotient left by one bit.
  - Set the least significant bit of the quotient to zero.
  - If the remainder is greater than or equal to the divisor (`dvr`), subtract the divisor from the remainder and set the least significant bit of the quotient to one.
- The final value of the remainder and quotient should be output as the module's output.

You should assume that both `div` and `dvr` are positive integers and that `dvr` is not equal to zero. You should also ensure that the output is correct for all possible values of `div` and `dvr`.

module divider(
    input [7:0] div, // dividend
    input [7:0] dvr, // divisor
    input clk,
    output reg [7:0] quotient, // quotient
    output reg [7:0] remainder // remainder
);

    reg [7:0] rem; // remainder
    integer i;
    
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        rem = div; // initialize remainder to dividend
        
        for (i = 0; i < 8; i = i + 1) begin
            remainder <= rem; // output remainder
            
            rem = rem << 1; // shift remainder left by 1 bit
            rem[0] = div[7]; // set least significant bit of remainder to most significant bit of dividend
            quotient = quotient << 1; // shift quotient left by 1 bit
            quotient[0] = 0; // set least significant bit of quotient to zero
            
            if (rem >= dvr) begin
                rem = rem - dvr; // subtract divisor from remainder
                quotient[0] = 1; // set least significant bit of quotient to one
            end
        end
        
        remainder <= rem; // output final remainder
    end
    
endmodule

In digital circuits, a multiplexer is a device that selects one of several input signals and forwards the selected input into a single output line. A multiplexer uses a control signal to determine which input signal should be forwarded to the output line. In this problem, you are tasked with designing a 2-to-1 multiplexer using Verilog HDL.

Your task is to write a Verilog module that implements a 2-to-1 multiplexer with the following inputs and outputs:

- `in0` (1-bit input): the first input signal
- `in1` (1-bit input): the second input signal
- `sel` (1-bit input): the control signal that selects which input signal should be forwarded to the output line
- `out` (1-bit output): the output signal that forwards the selected input signal

Your Verilog module should be named `mux_2to1` and should use the following syntax:

```
module mux_2to1 (
    input in0,
    input in1,
    input sel,
    output reg out
);
```

Your module should implement the 2-to-1 multiplexer using only the following gates:

- AND (`&`)
- OR (`|`)
- NOT (`~`)

You are not allowed to use any other Verilog modules or constructs in your implementation.
Response:
module mux_2to1 (
    input in0,
    input in1,
    input sel,
    output reg out
);

    always @(*) begin
        if (sel == 1'b0) begin
            out = in0;
        end else begin
            out = in1;
        end
    end

endmodule

- `data`: a 32-bit input representing the data to be written to the register bank.
- `rdaddress`: a 5-bit input representing the address of the register to be read.
- `wraddress`: a 5-bit input representing the address of the register to be written to.

  input clock,
  input [31:0] data,
  input [4:0] rdaddress,
  input [4:0] wraddress,
  input wren,

);

  wire [31:0] ram_data;

Please act as a professional Verilog designer. Your task is to create a Verilog module that implements a sequence detector state machine. 
A sequence detector state machine is a type of digital circuit that detects a specific sequence of input signals. 
The state machine has a set of states, and the transitions between states are determined by the input signals. 
When the state machine reaches the final state of the sequence, it outputs a signal to indicate that the sequence has been detected.
Your module should have the following inputs and outputs:

Inputs: a set of n input signals (in1, in2, ..., inn)
Outputs: a single output signal (detected)
The module should also have the following parameters:

n: the number of input signals
seq: the sequence to be detected (e.g., "1010" for a sequence of four bits)
Your module should implement the following functionality:

The circuit should have a set of states, each of which represents a portion of the sequence to be detected.
The transitions between states should be determined by the input signals.
When the state machine reaches the final state of the sequence, it should output a signal to indicate that the sequence has been detected.
To implement the sequence detector state machine, you should use Verilog code to define the states and transitions as a state machine. 
You should then use the input signals to determine the transitions between states. 
Finally, you should use the final state of the sequence to output a signal to indicate that the sequence has been detected.
Response:
module seq_detector (
  input [n-1:0] in,
  output detected
);

parameter n = 4; // number of input signals
parameter seq = "1010"; // sequence to be detected

reg [3:0] state; // state register
reg [3:0] next_state; // next state register
wire match; // signal to indicate a match

assign detected = (state == 3); // output signal when final state is reached

always @(*) begin
  case (state)
    0: begin // initial state
      if (in == seq[0]) begin
        next_state = 1;
      end else begin
        next_state = 0;
      end
    end
    1: begin // second state
      if (in == seq[1]) begin
        next_state = 2;
      end else if (in == seq[0]) begin
        next_state = 1;
      end else begin
        next_state = 0;
      end
    end
    2: begin // third state
      if (in == seq[2]) begin
        next_state = 3;
      end else if (in == seq[0]) begin
        next_state = 1;
      end else begin
        next_state = 0;
      end
    end
    3: begin // final state
      next_state = 3;
    end
  endcase
end

always @(posedge clk) begin
  state <= next_state; // update state register
end

endmodule

- Inputs: address (2-bit), areset (1-bit), clk (1-bit), read (1-bit), reset (1-bit), write (1-bit), writedata (32-bit)
- Outputs: c0 (1-bit), c1 (1-bit), locked (1-bit), phasedone (1-bit), readdata (32-bit)

The module should implement an Altera ALTPLL IP core with the following characteristics:

- The input clock (clk) should be connected to the ALTPLL IP core.
- The module should implement a standard synchronous interface (stdsync) to the ALTPLL IP core.
- The module should implement a 2-phase output clock (c0 and c1) from the ALTPLL IP core.
- The module should implement a locked output signal (locked) from the ALTPLL IP core.
- The module should implement a phasedone output signal (phasedone) from the ALTPLL IP core.
- The module should implement a read/write interface to access the following registers in the ALTPLL IP core:
  - pfdena (1-bit): power-down enable
  - pll_areset_in (1-bit): PLL asynchronous reset
- The module should implement a readdata output signal to return the following values:
  - pfdena (1-bit)
  - pll_areset_in (1-bit)
  - locked (1-bit)
  - phasedone (1-bit)

You should implement the module within 200 lines of Verilog code.
Response:
module my_pll (
  input wire [1:0] address,
  input wire areset,
  output wire c0,
  output wire c1,
  input wire clk,
  output wire locked,
  output wire phasedone,
  input wire read,
  output wire [31:0] readdata,
  input wire reset,
  input wire write,
  input wire [31:0] writedata
);

  // Instantiate the ALTPLL IP core
  wasca_altpll_0 altpll (
    .address(address),
    .areset(areset),
    .c0(c0),
    .c1(c1),
    .clk(clk),
    .locked(locked),
    .phasedone(phasedone),
    .read(read),
    .readdata(readdata),
    .reset(reset),
    .write(write),
    .writedata(writedata)
  );

  // Implement read/write interface
  reg [31:0] reg_pfdena = 1'b1;
  reg reg_pll_areset_in;
  always @(posedge clk) begin
    if (reset) begin
      reg_pfdena <= 1'b1;
    end else if (write && address == 2'b00) begin
      reg_pfdena[0] <= writedata[0];
    end else if (write && address == 2'b01) begin
      reg_pll_areset_in <= writedata[0];
    end
  end

  // Implement readdata output
  always @(*) begin
    readdata = {28'b0, reg_pfdena[0], reg_pll_areset_in, locked, phasedone};
  end

endmodule

- `RST`: a synchronous reset signal
- `CLK`: a clock signal
- `ENA`: an enable signal
- `RGA`: an 8-bit register
- `RGB`: an 8-bit register
- `RGZ`: an 8-bit wire
- `KEY`: a 2-bit register

The `protection` module should implement the following functionality:
- On the rising edge of `CLK` and if `ENA` is high, the value of `RGA` should be transferred to `RGB`.
- On the falling edge of `CLK` and if `ENA` is high, the value of `RGB` should be transferred to `RGZ`.
- If `KEY` is 2'b00, the output `RGZ` should be the bitwise AND of `RGA` and `RGB`.
- If `KEY` is 2'b01, the output `RGZ` should be the bitwise OR of `RGA` and `RGB`.
- If `KEY` is 2'b10, the output `RGZ` should be the bitwise XOR of `RGA` and `RGB`.
- If `KEY` is 2'b11, the output `RGZ` should be the bitwise complement of `RGA`.

Implement the `protection` module to satisfy the above requirements.
Response:
module protection(
  input RST,
  input CLK,
  input ENA,
  input [7:0] RGA,
  input [7:0] RGB,
  output [7:0] RGZ,
  input [1:0] KEY
);

  reg [7:0] RGB_reg;
  reg [7:0] RGZ_reg;

  always @(posedge CLK) begin
    if (ENA) begin
      RGB_reg <= RGA;
    end
  end

  always @(negedge CLK) begin
    if (ENA) begin
      RGZ_reg <= RGB;
    end
  end

  assign RGZ = (KEY == 2'b00) ? (RGA & RGB_reg) :
               (KEY == 2'b01) ? (RGA | RGB_reg) :
               (KEY == 2'b10) ? (RGA ^ RGB_reg) :
               (~RGA);

  always @(posedge CLK, negedge RST) begin
    if (RST == 0) begin
      RGB_reg <= 8'b0;
      RGZ_reg <= 8'b0;
    end
  end

endmodule

module dual_port_ram(
    input clk1, // clock input for port 1
    input clk2, // clock input for port 2
    input we1, // write enable input for port 1
    input we2, // write enable input for port 2
    input re1, // read enable input for port 1
    input re2, // read enable input for port 2
    input [3:0] addr1, // address input for port 1
    input [3:0] addr2, // address input for port 2
    input [7:0] data1, // data input for port 1
    input [7:0] data2, // data input for port 2
    output [7:0] q1, // data output for port 1
    output [7:0] q2 // data output for port 2
);

reg [7:0] mem [0:15]; // 16x8-bit memory

always @(posedge clk1) begin
    if (we1) begin // write to memory for port 1
        mem[addr1] <= data1;
    end
    if (re1) begin // read from memory for port 1
        q1 <= mem[addr1];
    end
end

always @(posedge clk2) begin
    if (we2) begin // write to memory for port 2
        mem[addr2] <= data2;
    end
    if (re2) begin // read from memory for port 2
        q2 <= mem[addr2];
    end
end

endmodule

Please act as a professional Verilog designer. Your task is to create a Verilog module that implements a First-In-First-Out (FIFO) memory block. 
A FIFO is a type of memory block that stores data in a queue-like structure, where the first data that is input is the first data that is output.
Your module should have the following inputs and outputs:

Inputs: 
- clk: the clock signal
- rst: the reset signal
- wr_en: the write enable signal
- rd_en: the read enable signal
- data_in: the data to be written to the FIFO

Outputs:
- data_out: the data read from the FIFO

The module should also have the following parameters:

- width: the width of the data bus in bits
- depth: the number of data elements that can be stored in the FIFO

Your module should implement the following functionality:

- When rst is high, the FIFO should be reset and all stored data should be cleared.
- When wr_en is high and the FIFO is not full, data_in should be written to the FIFO.
- When rd_en is high and the FIFO is not empty, data_out should be the first data element that was written to the FIFO.
- The FIFO should signal when it is full or empty.

To implement the FIFO, you should use Verilog code to define a memory array with depth elements and width bits per element.

The CIC decimator architecture consists of N integrator stages, followed by a decimation stage, and then N comb stages. Each integrator stage integrates the input signal over M samples, and each comb stage subtracts the delayed output of the previous stage from the current stage's output. The decimation stage simply outputs every RMAX-th sample.

You have been hired by a company to design a new module for their system. The module should be able to take in a data signal and output a processed signal. The module should also have power inputs for various voltage levels. You must design a verilog module that meets these requirements.

- `VPWR` is high (1)
- `VGND` is low (0)
- `VNB` is low (0)

module data_processing_module (
    input data_in,
    input [3:0] power_in,
    output reg data_out
);

    always @(*) begin
        if (data_in == 1'b1) begin
            if (power_in == 4'b1010) begin
                data_out <= 1'b1;
            end
            else begin
                data_out <= 1'bx;
            end
        end
        else begin
            if (power_in == 4'b1010) begin
                data_out <= 1'b0;
            end
            else begin
                data_out <= 1'bx;
            end
        end
    end

endmodule

module echo_cancel (
  input [n-1:0] in,
  input [n-1:0] rin,
  output [n-1:0] out
);

parameter n = 4; // number of input signals

reg [n-1:0] delay_line; // delay line for received signal

always @(posedge clk) begin
  delay_line <= rin;
end

assign out = in - delay_line; // subtract delayed signal from original signal

endmodule

Please act as a professional Verilog designer. Your task is to create a Verilog module that implements a pulse generator. 
There are two types of pulse generators: monostable and astable. 

A monostable pulse generator produces a single output pulse when triggered by an input signal. 
The duration of the pulse is determined by a resistor and a capacitor in the circuit. 
The inputs to the circuit are a trigger signal and a reset signal, and the output is a single pulse.

An astable pulse generator produces a continuous stream of output pulses. 
The frequency of the pulses is determined by a resistor and a capacitor in the circuit. 
The inputs to the circuit are a start signal and a stop signal, and the output is a stream of pulses.

Your module should have the following inputs and outputs:

Inputs: 
- For monostable pulse generator: trigger, reset
- For astable pulse generator: start, stop
- R, C: resistance and capacitance values used in the pulse generator circuit

Outputs: 
- For monostable pulse generator: out
- For astable pulse generator: out

Your module should also have the following parameters:

- type: the type of pulse generator (monostable or astable)
- freq: the frequency of the pulses (only for astable pulse generator)

Your module should implement the following functionality:
- For monostable pulse generator:
    - When the trigger input is high, the module should output a single pulse with a duration determined by the R and C values.
    - If the reset input is high before the pulse has finished, the module should immediately stop the pulse and reset the circuit.
- For astable pulse generator:
    - When the start input is high, the module should start producing a continuous stream of pulses with a frequency determined by the R and C values.
    - If the stop input is high, the module should immediately stop the pulse stream and reset the circuit.

To implement the pulse generator, you should use Verilog code to define the circuit based on the type of pulse generator and the input/output requirements. 
You should then use these functions to connect the inputs and outputs to the circuit, and ensure that the pulse generator functions properly according to the above requirements.

module pulse_generator (
  input trigger,
  input reset,
  input start,
  input stop,
  input R,
  input C,
  output out
);

parameter type = "monostable"; // pulse generator type (monostable or astable)
parameter freq = 100; // pulse frequency (only for astable pulse generator)

reg pulse; // output pulse signal
reg astable_pulse; // output pulse signal for astable pulse generator
reg [31:0] counter; // counter for astable pulse generator

always @ (posedge trigger or posedge reset) begin
  if (reset) begin
    pulse <= 0;
  end else if (trigger) begin
    pulse <= 1'b1;
    #((R*C)*2); // pulse duration determined by R and C values
    pulse <= 0;
  end
end

always @ (posedge start or posedge stop) begin
  if (stop) begin
    astable_pulse <= 0;
    counter <= 0;
  end else if (start) begin
    counter <= counter + 1;
    if (counter == ((1/(freq*(R*C)))/2)) begin // pulse frequency determined by R, C, and freq values
      astable_pulse <= ~astable_pulse;
      counter <= 0;
    end
  end
end

assign out = (type == "monostable") ? pulse : astable_pulse;

endmodule

);

module bitwise_operations (
    input [7:0] in1, // First 8-bit input
    input [7:0] in2, // Second 8-bit input
    output [7:0] xor_output, // Bitwise XOR of the two inputs and the output of the first functional module
    output [7:0] and_output, // Bitwise AND of the two inputs
    output [7:0] not_output // Bitwise NOT of the first input
);

    assign and_output = in1 & in2; // Bitwise AND of the two inputs
    assign not_output = ~in1; // Bitwise NOT of the first input

endmodule

module top_module (
    input clk, // Clock input for synchronous reset
    input reset, // Synchronous active-high reset
    input [7:0] in1, // First 8-bit input
    input [7:0] in2, // Second 8-bit input
    output [7:0] out, // Bitwise XOR of the two inputs and the output of the first functional module
    output [7:0] and_output, // Bitwise AND of the two inputs
    output [7:0] not_output // Bitwise NOT of the first input
);

    bitwise_operations bitwise_ops(in1, in2, and_output, not_output, xor_output);

    reg [7:0] xor_output_reg; // Register for storing the XOR output
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (reset) begin
            xor_output_reg <= 8'b0; // Reset the register to 0
        end else begin
            xor_output_reg <= xor_output ^ and_output; // Bitwise XOR of the two inputs and the output of the first functional module
        end
    end

    assign out = xor_output_reg; // Output the XOR output from the register

endmodule

You have been asked to design a Verilog module that generates a VGA signal for a 640x480 display. The module should have the following inputs and outputs:

Inputs:
- `clk`: a 25MHz clock signal
- `rst`: a reset signal

Outputs:
- `addr`: a 19-bit address signal that represents the current pixel being displayed on the screen
- `v_active`: a signal that indicates whether the VGA signal is currently outputting an active pixel (as opposed to a blanking period)
- `h_sync`: a signal that indicates whether the VGA signal is currently outputting a horizontal synchronization pulse
- `v_sync`: a signal that indicates whether the VGA signal is currently outputting a vertical synchronization pulse

Your module should have two counters: `h_count` and `v_count`. `h_count` should count from 0 to 799, and `v_count` should count from 0 to 524. The counters should reset to 0 when `rst` is high. 

Your module should also generate the following signals:
- `h_sync`: this should be high during the horizontal synchronization pulse. The pulse should last for 96 pixels, starting at pixel 799 and ending at pixel 0.
- `v_sync`: this should be high during the vertical synchronization pulse. The pulse should last for 2 lines, starting at line 524 and ending at line 0.
- `v_active`: this should be high during the active portion of the screen. The active portion of the screen should be from pixel 143 to pixel 782 (a total of 640 pixels) and from line 35 to line 514 (a total of 480 lines).

Finally, your module should generate the `addr` signal. This should be a 19-bit signal that represents the current pixel being displayed on the screen. The most significant bit should represent the current row, and the least significant bit should represent the current column. 

Write a Verilog module that implements the VGA signal generator described above.
Response:
module vga_core(
                vga_clk, 
                rst, 
                addr,
                v_active,
                h_sync, 
                v_sync
                );

	input              	vga_clk;                // 25MHz
	input              	rst;
	output     	[18: 0] addr;                   // pixel Screen address, 640 (1024) x 480 (512)
	output             	v_active;               // read VRAM RAM (active_low)
	output             	h_sync, v_sync;         // horizontal and vertical synchronization

	// h_count: VGA horizontal counter (0-799)
	reg [9:0] h_count = 0; // VGA horizontal counter (0-799): pixels
	always @ (posedge vga_clk or posedge rst) begin
		if (rst) begin
			h_count <= 10'h0;
		end else if (h_count == 10'd799) begin
			h_count <= 10'h0;
		end else begin
			h_count <= h_count + 10'h1;
		end
	end

	// v_count: VGA vertical counter (0-524)
	reg [9:0] v_count = 0; // VGA vertical counter (0-524): lines
	always @ (posedge vga_clk or posedge rst) begin
		if (rst) begin
			v_count <= 10'h0;
		end else if (h_count == 10'd799) begin
			if (v_count == 10'd524) begin
				v_count <= 10'h0;
			end else begin
				v_count <= v_count + 10'h1;
			end
		end
	end

	// signal timing
	wire h_sync 		= (h_count > 10'd95);          // 96 -> 799
	wire v_sync 		= (v_count > 10'd1);           // 2 -> 524
	wire v_active 		= (h_count > 10'd142) &&     // 143 -> 782
						  (h_count < 10'd783) &&     // 640 pixels
						  (v_count > 10'd34) &&      // 35 -> 514
						  (v_count < 10'd515);       // 480 lines

	wire [ 9: 0] col   	= h_count - 10'd143;    // pixel Screen addr col
	wire [ 9: 0] row   	= v_count - 10'd35;     // pixel Screen addr row
	wire [18: 0] addr  	= {row[ 8: 0], col};    // pixel Screen addr

endmodule

module dual_port_ram (
  input clk,
  input write_en_1,
  input write_en_2,
  input [log2(depth)-1:0] addr_1,
  input [log2(depth)-1:0] addr_2,
  input [width-1:0] data_in_1,
  input [width-1:0] data_in_2,
  input read_en_1,
  input read_en_2,
  output reg [width-1:0] data_out_1,
  output reg [width-1:0] data_out_2
);

parameter depth = 256; // depth of memory block
parameter width = 8; // width of memory block (number of bits in each memory location)

reg [width-1:0] mem [0:depth-1]; // array of memory locations

// Write operations
always @(posedge clk) begin
  if (write_en_1) begin
    mem[addr_1] <= data_in_1;
  end
  if (write_en_2) begin
    mem[addr_2] <= data_in_2;
  end
end

// Read operations
always @(posedge clk) begin
  if (read_en_1) begin
    data_out_1 <= mem[addr_1];
  end
  if (read_en_2) begin
    data_out_2 <= mem[addr_2];
  end
end

endmodule

Design a system that combines the ripple carry adder and matrix multiplication modules. The system should take two 4x4 matrices of 16-bit integers (A[3:0][3:0] and B[3:0][3:0]) as inputs and perform a matrix multiplication using the matrix_mult module. The output of the matrix multiplication should be fed into the ripple carry adder module along with a constant value of 0x1234 as input A and the output of the previous stage as input B. The output of the ripple carry adder should be the final output of the system. The ripple carry adder should have overflow detection, and if the sum of the two inputs and the carry-in is greater than 1111 in binary, the output carry-out should be high to indicate overflow.
Response:
module ripple_matrix_mult_adder (
    input [15:0] A [3:0][3:0], // 4x4 matrix of 16-bit integers
    input [15:0] B [3:0][3:0], // 4x4 matrix of 16-bit integers
    input [15:0] constant, // constant value of 0x1234
    input clk, // clock input
    input reset, // Synchronous active-high reset
    output reg [15:0] q // output of the final stage
);

    wire [15:0] mult_out [3:0][3:0]; // output of matrix multiplication
    wire [15:0] adder_out [3:0][3:0]; // output of ripple carry adder

    matrix_mult mult_inst (
        .A(A),
        .B(B),
        .C(mult_out),
        .clk(clk),
        .reset(reset)
    );

    genvar i, j;
    generate
        for (i = 0; i < 4; i = i + 1) begin : gen_rows
            for (j = 0; j < 4; j = j + 1) begin : gen_cols
                ripple_adder adder_inst (
                    .A(constant),
                    .B(mult_out[i][j]),
                    .C(adder_out[i][j]),
                    .CI(adder_out[i-1][j+1][15]), // carry-in from previous stage
                    .CO(adder_out[i][j][15]) // carry-out for overflow detection
                );
            end
        end
    endgenerate

    assign q = adder_out[3][3]; // output of final stage

endmodule

module ripple_adder (
    input [15:0] A, // input A
    input [15:0] B, // input B
    output reg [15:0] C, // output C
    input CI, // carry-in
    output reg CO // carry-out
);

    always @(A, B, CI) begin
        C = A + B + CI;
        CO = (C > 16'h1111) ? 1'b1 : 1'b0; // overflow detection
    end

endmodule

module matrix_mult (
    input [15:0] A [3:0][3:0], // 4x4 matrix of 16-bit integers
    input [15:0] B [3:0][3:0], // 4x4 matrix of 16-bit integers
    output reg [15:0] C [3:0][3:0], // output matrix
    input clk, // clock input
    input reset // Synchronous active-high reset
);

    integer i, j, k;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (reset) begin
            for (i = 0; i < 4; i = i + 1) begin
                for (j = 0; j < 4; j = j + 1) begin
                    C[i][j] <= 16'h0000;
                end
            end
        end else begin
            for (i = 0; i < 4; i = i + 1) begin
                for (j = 0; j < 4; j = j + 1) begin
                    for (k = 0; k < 4; k = k + 1) begin
                        C[i][j] <= C[i][j] + A[i][k] * B[k][j];
                    end
                end
            end
        end
    end

module up_down_counter (
    input clk,
    input rst_n,
    input up_down,
    input [3:0] load_data,
    output reg [3:0] count
);

reg [3:0] count_reg1, count_reg2;

always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
    if (~rst_n) begin
        count_reg1 <= 4'b0000;
        count_reg2 <= 4'b0000;
    end
    else begin
        count_reg1 <= count_reg2;
        count_reg2 <= count;
    end
end

always @(*) begin
    if (up_down) begin
        if (load_data != 4'b0000) begin
            count = load_data;
        end
        else begin
            count = count_reg1 + 4'b0001;
        end
    end
    else begin
        if (load_data != 4'b0000) begin
            count = load_data;
        end
        else begin
            count = count_reg1 - 4'b0001;
        end
    end
end

endmodule

module alu (
    input [3:0] a,
    input [3:0] b,
    input [2:0] op,
    output reg [3:0] out
);

    always @(*) begin
        case(op)
            3'b000: out = a + b; // addition
            3'b001: out = a - b; // subtraction
            3'b010: out = a & b; // bitwise AND
            3'b011: out = a | b; // bitwise OR
            3'b100: out = a ^ b; // bitwise XOR
            3'b101: out = a << 1; // shift left
            default: out = 4'b0; // default output
        endcase
    end

endmodule

The input 'a' should be connected directly to the output, 'b' should be inverted and then connected to the output, and 'c' should be connected to the output through an AND gate with 'd' as the other input. The comparator module should compare two 4-bit binary numbers and output a binary one if they are equal and a binary zero otherwise. The system should incorporate an additional module that takes in the output of the multiplexer module and the output of the comparator module to generate a final output. The final output should be the result of the comparison of 'e' with either the output of the multiplexer module or its inverse, depending on the value of 'f'.
Response:
module multiplexer (
    input [3:0] a,b,c,d, // Input ports for the multiplexer
    input sel, // Input port to select which input to output
    output reg [3:0] out // Output port for the multiplexer
);

always @* begin
    case(sel)
        2'b00: out = a; // Output 'a' when sel is 00
        2'b01: out = ~b; // Output inverted 'b' when sel is 01
        2'b10: out = c & d; // Output 'c' AND 'd' when sel is 10
        default: out = 4'b0; // Output 0 for all other cases
    endcase
end

endmodule

module comparator (
    input [3:0] in1, in2, // Input ports for the comparator
    output reg out // Output port for the comparator
);

always @* begin
    if(in1 == in2) begin // If inputs are equal
        out = 1'b1; // Output 1
    end else begin // If inputs are not equal
        out = 1'b0; // Output 0
    end
end

endmodule

module final_module (
    input in, // Input port for the comparator output
    input sel, // Input port to select which output of the multiplexer module to use for comparison
    input [3:0] e, // Input port for the binary number
    output reg out // Output port for the final output
);

reg [3:0] mux_out; // Internal wire to store the output of the multiplexer module

multiplexer mux(.a(a),.b(b),.c(c),.d(d),.sel(sel),.out(mux_out)); // Instantiate the multiplexer module
comparator comp(.in1(mux_out),.in2(~mux_out),.out(comp_out)); // Instantiate the comparator module

always @* begin
    if(f == 1'b0) begin // If 'f' is 0
        if(in == e) begin // If comparator output is equal to 'e'
            out = 1'b1; // Output 1
        end else begin // If comparator output is not equal to 'e'
            out = 1'b0; // Output 0
        end
    end else begin // If 'f' is 1
        if(in == ~mux_out) begin // If comparator output is equal to inverted multiplexer output
            out = 1'b1; // Output 1
        end else begin // If comparator output is not equal to inverted multiplexer output
            out = 1'b0; // Output 0
        end
    end
end

endmodule

module top_module ( 
    input [3:0] e, // Input port for the binary number
    input f, // Input port to select which output of the multiplexer module to use for comparison
    input [3:0] a,b,c,d, // Inputs for the multiplexer module
    output out // Final output port
); 

final_module final(.in(comp_out),.sel(f),.e(e),.out(out)); // Instantiate the final module

endmodule

module mux_pipeline(
    input a,
    input b,
    input sel_b1,
    input sel_b2,
    input clk,
    output reg out_always
);

reg mux_out1;
reg mux_out2;

always @(posedge clk) begin
    mux_out1 <= (sel_b1 & sel_b2) ? b : a;
end

always @(posedge clk) begin
    mux_out2 <= mux_out1;
end

always @(posedge clk) begin
    out_always <= mux_out2;
end

endmodule

module top_module(
    input a,
    input b,
    input sel_b1,
    input sel_b2,
    input clk,
    output reg out_always
);

mux_pipeline mux_inst(
    .a(a),
    .b(b),
    .sel_b1(sel_b1),
    .sel_b2(sel_b2),
    .clk(clk),
    .out_always(out_always)
);

endmodule

input clk;          // clock input
input resetn;       // reset input
input en;           // enable input
input [31:0] d;     // data input

end

endmodule

module RAM_16384x36(

    input rst_a,
    input rst_b,
    input [13:0] addr_a,
    input [13:0] addr_b,
    input [35:0] data_a,
    input [35:0] data_b,
    input we_a,
    input we_b,
    input re_a,
    input re_b,
    output reg [35:0] q_a,
    output reg [35:0] q_b
);

reg [35:0] ram [0:16383];

always @(posedge clk) begin
    if (rst_a) begin
        q_a <= 36'h00000000;
    end else if (re_a) begin
        q_a <= ram[addr_a];
    end else if (we_a) begin
        ram[addr_a] <= data_a;
    end
    
    if (rst_b) begin
        q_b <= 36'h00000000;
    end else if (re_b) begin
        q_b <= ram[addr_b];
    end else if (we_b) begin
        ram[addr_b] <= data_b;
    end
end

endmodule

module pattern_detector (
    input [7:0] in,
    output reg [2:0] pos_dec
);

    reg [3:0] pattern = 4'b1101; // Define the 4-bit pattern to detect
    
    wire [3:0] match; // Create a wire to store the match result
    
    assign match = in & pattern; // Perform bitwise AND to detect the pattern
    
    priority_encoder pe(match, pos_dec); // Use a priority encoder to find the position of the most significant bit in the pattern
    
    always @(*) begin
        if (match == pattern) // If the pattern is present in the input vector
            pos_dec = pos_dec + 1; // Increment the position by 1 to account for the 0-indexing of the priority encoder
        else
            pos_dec = 0; // If the pattern is not present, set the position to 0
    end
    
endmodule

module shift_register(
    input clk,
    input areset,  // async active-high reset to zero
    input load,
    input ena,
    input [3:0] data,
    output reg [3:0] q);

    reg [3:0] q_temp;

    always @(posedge clk, posedge areset) begin
        if (areset) begin
            q_temp <= 4'b0;
        end else if (load && ena) begin
            q_temp <= data;
        end else if (ena) begin
            q_temp <= {q_temp[2:0], 1'b0};
        end
    end

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (areset) begin
            q <= 4'b0;
        end else begin
            q <= q_temp;
        end
    end

endmodule

- The module should use the control signal to determine the duty cycle of the PWM signal. The duty cycle should be equal to ctrl/MAXVAL.
- The module should compare the counter value with the duty cycle and output a high signal when the counter value is less than the duty cycle, and a low signal otherwise.

To implement the PWM, you should use Verilog code to define the counter, the duty cycle calculation, and the comparison between the counter and the duty cycle. You should then use these functions to generate the PWM signal.

module PWM (
  input clk,
  input [7:0] ctrl,
  output pwm
);

parameter MAXVAL = 255; // maximum value of the counter

reg [7:0] counter = 0; // initialize the counter to 0

assign pwm = (counter < (ctrl * MAXVAL / 255)) ? 1'b1 : 1'b0; // compare the counter value with the duty cycle and output a high signal when the counter value is less than the duty cycle, and a low signal otherwise.

always @(posedge clk) begin
  counter <= (counter == MAXVAL) ? 0 : counter + 1; // use the clock signal to generate a counter that counts from 0 to a maximum value (MAXVAL) and then resets to 0.
end

endmodule

When an interrupt request signal is received, the controller block should determine which priority level the interrupt request belongs to based on the priority of the interrupt sources.
If the interrupt request is of higher priority than the current interrupt being serviced, the controller block should generate an interrupt acknowledge signal for the new interrupt request and halt the current interrupt service routine.
If the interrupt request is of lower priority than the current interrupt being serviced, the controller block should ignore the interrupt request.
If multiple interrupt requests are received at the same time, the controller block should service the interrupt with the highest priority first.
To implement the interrupt controller block, you should use Verilog code to define the priority levels and use them to prioritize the interrupt requests. 
You should then use the priority levels to generate the interrupt acknowledge signals.
Finally, you should use the reset signal to reset the interrupt controller block to its initial state.
Response:
module InterruptController (
  input [n-1:0] irq,
  input reset,
  output [m-1:0] ack
);

parameter n = 4; // number of interrupt request signals
parameter m = 2; // number of interrupt acknowledge signals
parameter p = 3; // number of interrupt priority levels

reg [n-1:0] irq_priority; // priority level of each interrupt request
reg [n-1:0] irq_pending; // pending interrupt requests
reg [n-1:0] irq_serviced; // currently serviced interrupt requests
reg [m-1:0] ack_priority; // priority level of each interrupt acknowledge
reg [m-1:0] ack_pending; // pending interrupt acknowledges
reg [m-1:0] ack_serviced; // currently serviced interrupt acknowledges

// initialize interrupt controller block
initial begin
  irq_priority = {p{1'b0}}; // set all interrupt priorities to 0
  irq_pending = {n{1'b0}}; // clear all pending interrupts
  irq_serviced = {n{1'b0}}; // clear all serviced interrupts
  ack_priority = {p{1'b0}}; // set all acknowledge priorities to 0
  ack_pending = {m{1'b0}}; // clear all pending acknowledges
  ack_serviced = {m{1'b0}}; // clear all serviced acknowledges
end

// assign interrupt priorities based on interrupt sources
always @(*) begin
  for (i = 0; i < n; i = i + 1) begin
    case (i)
      // assign priority level for each interrupt source
      // higher priority levels have lower numbers
      0: irq_priority[i] = 2'b00; // interrupt source 0 has highest priority
      1: irq_priority[i] = 2'b01; // interrupt source 1 has medium priority
      2: irq_priority[i] = 2'b10; // interrupt source 2 has lowest priority
      3: irq_priority[i] = 2'b10; // interrupt source 3 has lowest priority
      default: irq_priority[i] = 2'b11; // unused interrupt sources have lowest priority
    endcase
  end
end

// generate interrupt acknowledges based on interrupt priorities
always @(*) begin
  for (j = 0; j < m; j = j + 1) begin
    ack_priority[j] = {p{1'b0}}; // clear acknowledge priority for each acknowledge signal
    ack_pending[j] = 1'b0; // clear pending acknowledge for each acknowledge signal
    ack_serviced[j] = 1'b0; // clear serviced acknowledge for each acknowledge signal
    for (i = 0; i < n; i = i + 1) begin
      if (irq[i] && !irq_serviced[i]) begin // check if interrupt request is pending and not already serviced
        if (irq_priority[i] < ack_priority[j]) begin // check if interrupt request has higher priority than current acknowledge
          ack_priority[j] = irq_priority[i]; // set acknowledge priority to interrupt priority
          ack_pending[j] = 1'b1; // set pending acknowledge for current acknowledge signal
        end
      end
    end
  end
end

// service interrupts based on acknowledge priorities
always @(*) begin
  for (i = 0; i < n; i = i + 1) begin
    if (irq[i] && !irq_pending[i] && !irq_serviced[i]) begin // check if interrupt request is not already pending or serviced
      irq_pending[i] = 1'b1; // set interrupt request as pending
      for (j = 0; j < m; j = j + 1) begin
        if (ack_pending[j]) begin // check if acknowledge signal is pending
          if (ack_priority[j] < irq_priority[i]) begin // check if acknowledge signal has higher priority than interrupt request
            ack_serviced[j] = 1'b1; // set acknowledge signal as serviced
            irq_serviced[i] = 1'b1; // set interrupt request as serviced
          end
        end
      end
    end
  end
end

// reset interrupt controller block
always @(posedge reset) begin
  irq_priority = {p{1'b0}}; // set all interrupt priorities to 0
  irq_pending = {n{1'b0}}; // clear all pending interrupts
  irq_serviced = {n{1'b0}}; // clear all serviced interrupts
  ack_priority = {p{1'b0}}; // set all acknowledge priorities to 0
  ack_pending = {m{1'b0}}; // clear all pending acknowledges
  ack_serviced = {m{1'b0}}; // clear all serviced acknowledges
end

// assign acknowledge signals based on pending acknowledges
assign ack = ~ack_pending;

endmodule

1. The most significant bit (MSB) of the Gray code is equal to the MSB of the binary number.
2. For each subsequent bit in the Gray code, it is equal to the exclusive OR (XOR) of the corresponding bit and the previous bit in the binary number.

1. The MSB of the Gray code is equal to the MSB of the binary number, which is `1`.
2. The second bit of the Gray code is equal to the XOR of the second and first bits of the binary number, which is `0 XOR 1 = 1`.
3. The third bit of the Gray code is equal to the XOR of the third and second bits of the binary number, which is `1 XOR 0 = 1`.

You are tasked with designing a FIFO (First-In-First-Out) memory generator in Verilog. The FIFO memory should be able to store 94-bit data and have a capacity of 64 words. The memory should have two ports: one for writing data into the memory and another for reading data out of the memory. The FIFO memory should operate in a synchronous manner, with the read and write operations being synchronized to a common clock signal.

You should design a single module that implements the FIFO memory generator. The module should have the following input and output ports:

- `clk`: the clock signal
- `din`: the input data to be written into the memory
- `wr_en`: write enable signal; when high, data should be written into the memory
- `rd_en`: read enable signal; when high, data should be read from the memory
- `dout`: the output data read from the memory

You should implement the FIFO memory using a circular buffer. The circular buffer should be implemented using a single block RAM module with a capacity of 6,016 bits. You should use the `fifo_generator_1blk_mem_gen_top` module as a starting point for your design.

Your solution should consist of a single Verilog module with a maximum of 200 lines of code. You should not use any Verilog libraries or built-in FIFO modules.

module fifo_memory_generator
  (dout,
   clk,
   wr_en,
   rd_en,
   din);

  output [93:0] dout;
  input clk;
  input wr_en;
  input rd_en;
  input [93:0] din;

  // Define constants
  parameter WIDTH = 94; // Data width
  parameter DEPTH = 64; // Depth of FIFO
  parameter ADDR_WIDTH = $clog2(DEPTH); // Address width
  parameter MEM_WIDTH = WIDTH + ADDR_WIDTH; // Width of memory
  parameter MEM_DEPTH = DEPTH + 1; // Depth of memory

  // Define signals
  reg [MEM_WIDTH-1:0] memory [0:MEM_DEPTH-1]; // Memory
  reg [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] wr_ptr = 0; // Write pointer
  reg [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] rd_ptr = 0; // Read pointer
  reg [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] next_wr_ptr = 0; // Next write pointer
  reg [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] next_rd_ptr = 0; // Next read pointer
  wire [MEM_WIDTH-1:0] rd_data = memory[rd_ptr]; // Data read from memory

  // Write logic
  always @(posedge clk) begin
    if (wr_en) begin
      memory[wr_ptr] <= {din, wr_ptr}; // Write data to memory
      next_wr_ptr <= wr_ptr + 1; // Update next write pointer
    end
  end

  // Read logic
  always @(posedge clk) begin
    if (rd_en) begin
      dout <= rd_data[WIDTH-1:0]; // Output data
      next_rd_ptr <= rd_ptr + 1; // Update next read pointer
    end
  end

  // Update pointers
  always @(posedge clk) begin
    wr_ptr <= next_wr_ptr;
    rd_ptr <= next_rd_ptr;
  end

endmodule

module mem_encrypt_decrypt (
  input clk,
  input we,
  input [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] din,
  input [KEY_WIDTH-1:0] key,
  input [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] addr,
  output reg [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] dout
);

parameter KEY_WIDTH = 8; // width of the key
parameter ADDR_WIDTH = 8; // width of the address bus

- A write operation is initiated by asserting `address` to the desired register address and `in_port` to the desired data. The data should be written to the register on the rising edge of the clock signal.
- A read operation is initiated by asserting `address` to the desired register address. The data read from the register should be available on the `readdata` output on the rising edge of the clock signal.

module pio (
  input [1:0] address,
  input clk,
  input [7:0] in_port,
  input reset_n,
  output reg [31:0] readdata
);

  reg [31:0] reg_data; // register to store data

  always @(posedge clk or negedge reset_n) begin
    if (~reset_n) begin
      reg_data <= 0;
      readdata <= 0;
    end
    else begin
      if (address == 2'b00) begin // write operation
        reg_data <= in_port;
      end
      else if (address == 2'b01) begin // read operation
        readdata <= reg_data;
      end
    end
  end

endmodule

module counter (

  input rst_n,
  input en,
  output reg [3:0] out
);

      out <= 4'b0;
    end else if (en) begin
      out <= out + 1;
    end
  end

You are tasked with designing a verilog module that implements a 4-bit counter that can count up or down based on a control signal. Additionally, the counter should be able to count in increments of 1 or 2 based on another control signal. The module should have an enable signal to start and stop the counter and a synchronous reset signal to reset the counter to 0. 

The module should have the following input and output ports:

- `input logic clk`: clock signal
- `input logic rst`: synchronous reset signal
- `input logic up_down`: control signal for up/down counting (0 for up, 1 for down)
- `input logic count_by_two`: control signal for counting in increments of 1 or 2 (0 for 1, 1 for 2)
- `input logic enable`: enable signal to start and stop the counter
- `output logic [3:0] counter_out`: 4-bit counter output

Assume that the counter starts at 0 and counts up by default.

module counter
  (input logic clk,
   input logic rst,
   input logic up_down,
   input logic count_by_two,
   input logic enable,
   output logic [3:0] counter_out);

   // Declarations
   logic [3:0] counter_reg; // Registered version of counter_out

   always_ff @(posedge clk) begin
      if (rst) begin
         counter_reg <= 0;
      end
      else if (enable) begin
         if (up_down) begin
            if (count_by_two) begin
               counter_reg <= counter_reg - 2;
            end
            else begin
               counter_reg <= counter_reg - 1;
            end
         end
         else begin
            if (count_by_two) begin
               counter_reg <= counter_reg + 2;
            end
            else begin
               counter_reg <= counter_reg + 1;
            end
         end
      end
   end

   assign counter_out = counter_reg;

endmodule

module shift_register_4bit (

);

module calculator(
    input [3:0] A,
    input [3:0] B,
    input op,
    input clk,
    output reg [3:0] result,
    output reg overflow
);

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (op == 0) begin // addition
            result <= A + B;
        end else begin // subtraction
            result <= A - B;
        end
        
        if (result > 15) begin // check for overflow
            overflow <= 1;
        end else begin
            overflow <= 0;
        end
    end
    
endmodule

module mux_4to1_enable (
    input [7:0] D0,
    input [7:0] D1,
    input [7:0] D2,
    input [7:0] D3,
    input [1:0] SEL,
    input EN,
    output reg [7:0] q
);

always @(*) begin
    case (SEL)
        2'b00: q = EN ? D0 : 8'b0;
        2'b01: q = EN ? D1 : 8'b0;
        2'b10: q = EN ? D2 : 8'b0;
        2'b11: q = EN ? D3 : 8'b0;
    endcase
end

endmodule

module addsub_4bit (
    input [3:0] A,
    input [3:0] B,
    input M,
    output reg [3:0] q,
    output reg OV
);

always @(*) begin
    if (M == 1) begin
        q = A - B;
        OV = (q[3] != A[3] && q[3] != B[3]);
    end else begin
        q = A + B;
        OV = (q[3] == 1 && (A[3] == 0 || B[3] == 0));
    end
end

endmodule

module functional_module (
    input [7:0] mux_out,
    input [3:0] addsub_out,
    input [1:0] SEL,
    output reg [7:0] q
);

always @(*) begin
    case (SEL)
        2'b00: q = mux_out + addsub_out;
        2'b01: q = mux_out - addsub_out;
        default: q = 8'b0;
    endcase
end

endmodule

module control_logic (
    input [1:0] SEL1,
    input [1:0] SEL2,
    input [7:0] mux_out,
    input [3:0] addsub_out,
    input EN,
    output reg [7:0] q
);

wire [7:0] mux_q;
wire [7:0] func_q;

mux_4to1_enable mux_inst (
    .D0(D0),
    .D1(D1),
    .D2(D2),
    .D3(D3),
    .SEL(SEL1),
    .EN(EN),
    .q(mux_q)
);

addsub_4bit addsub_inst (
    .A(A),
    .B(B),
    .M(M),
    .q(addsub_out),
    .OV(OV)
);

functional_module func_inst (
    .mux_out(mux_q),
    .addsub_out(addsub_out),
    .SEL(SEL2),
    .q(func_q)
);

always @(*) begin
    if (SEL2 == 2'b10 || SEL2 == 2'b11) begin
        q = 8'b0;
    end else if (SEL1 == SEL2) begin
        q = mux_q;
    end else begin
        q = func_q;
    end
end

endmodule

    input reset,
    input [7:0] D0,
    input [7:0] D1,
    input [7:0] D2,

);

reg [3:0] addsub_out;
reg [7:0] mux_out;

control_logic control_inst (

    .SEL2(SEL2),
    .D0(D0),

    .D2(D2),
    .D3(D3),

The monitor module should track the credits available for transmitting Non-Posted (NP) traffic from the device to the host and notify the source logic when credits are available. The monitor module should be implemented in Verilog and should consist of a single module within 200 lines of code.

The monitor module should have the following inputs and outputs:

Inputs:
- clk_in: the clock input for the module.
- rstn: the active-low reset input for the module.

- np_sent: a single-bit input from the source logic indicating that an NP TLP (Transaction Layer Packet) is being issued from the source logic that is doing credit check gating.
- np_tx_sent: a single-bit input indicating that an NP TLP has been transmitted onto the AV-ST (Address-Value Streaming) interface.

Outputs:

The monitor module should implement the following state machine:
1. LATCH_CRED: In this state, the monitor module should latch the value of np_cred and grant credits to the source logic if np_cred is greater than 0. If np_cred is 0, the monitor module should stay in this state and set have_cred to 0.
2. GRANT_CRED: In this state, the monitor module should grant credits to the source logic until all credits are used. If np_sent is high and local_creds_avail is 1, the monitor module should transition to the WAIT_LAST_NP_TX state.
3. WAIT_LAST_NP_TX: In this state, the monitor module should wait for all NP TLPs to be transmitted on the AV-ST interface. Once all NP TLPs have been transmitted, the monitor module should transition to the WAIT_CRED_UPD state.
4. WAIT_CRED_UPD: In this state, the monitor module should wait for CRED_LAT clock cycles before transitioning back to the LATCH_CRED state.

- `b`: 32-bit input register B

module calculator(
    input [31:0] a,
    input [31:0] b,
    input [1:0] op,
    output reg [31:0] c
);

always @*
begin
    case(op)
        2'b00: c = a + b; // addition
        2'b01: c = a - b; // subtraction
        2'b10: c = a * b; // multiplication
        2'b11: c = a / b; // division
        default: c = 0;   // default to 0 if op is invalid
    endcase
end

endmodule

Your VGA buffer module should have the following inputs:

- `wen`: a write enable signal
- `x_addr_w`: a 10-bit input representing the X-coordinate of the pixel to be written
- `y_addr_w`: a 10-bit input representing the Y-coordinate of the pixel to be written
- `x_addr_r`: a 10-bit input representing the X-coordinate of the pixel to be read
- `y_addr_r`: a 10-bit input representing the Y-coordinate of the pixel to be read
- `data_w`: a 24-bit input representing the pixel color to be written

Your VGA buffer module should have the following output:
- `data_r`: a 24-bit output representing the pixel color to be read

Your VGA buffer module should store the pixel data in a memory array. The memory array should have a size of 1024x768, which corresponds to the resolution of the VGA display. The memory array should be initialized to all zeros.

Your VGA buffer module should support read and write operations. During a write operation, the module should write the pixel color specified by `data_w` to the memory location specified by `x_addr_w` and `y_addr_w`. During a read operation, the module should output the pixel color stored in the memory location specified by `x_addr_r` and `y_addr_r`.

Your VGA buffer module should operate at a frequency of 25MHz.

module vga_buffer(
  input clk_w,
  input clk_r,
  input wen,
  input [9:0] x_addr_w,
  input [9:0] y_addr_w,
  input [9:0] x_addr_r,
  input [9:0] y_addr_r,
  input [23:0] data_w,
  output [23:0] data_r
);

  reg [23:0] mem [0:767][0:1023]; // memory array for storing pixel data
  integer i, j; // loop variables for memory access

  always @(posedge clk_w) begin
    if (wen) begin
      mem[y_addr_w][x_addr_w] <= data_w; // write data to memory
    end
  end

  always @(posedge clk_r) begin
    data_r <= mem[y_addr_r][x_addr_r]; // read data from memory
  end

endmodule

module shift_register (
    input clk,
    input areset,
    input load,
    input ena,
    input [3:0] data,
    output [3:0] q
);

reg [3:0] q_reg;

always @(posedge clk or posedge areset) begin
    if (areset) begin
        q_reg <= 4'b0;
    end else if (load) begin
        q_reg <= data;
    end else if (ena) begin
        q_reg <= {q_reg[2:0], 1'b0};
    end
end

assign q = q_reg;

endmodule

    input [3:0] a,
    input [3:0] b,

);

);

always @(*) begin

    end else begin

    end
end

endmodule

Design a system that combines a 100-bit rotator and a 4-digit BCD counter. The rotator should have four input ports: clk, load, ena, and data. The load port should be used to load the shift register with data[99:0]. The ena[1:0] port should be used to choose the direction of rotation, where 2'b01 rotates right by one bit, 2'b10 rotates left by one bit, and 2'b00 and 2'b11 do not rotate. The output port q from the rotator should be connected to the input port of the BCD counter. 

The BCD counter should count from 0000 to 9999 in decimal, with an enable signal that indicates when each of the upper three digits should be incremented. Each decimal digit is encoded using 4 bits, where q[3:0] is the ones digit, q[7:4] is the tens digit, etc. The counter should have a synchronous active-high reset input port and a clock input port. 

The system should include an additional functional module that takes in the output from the BCD counter and the output from the rotator and calculates their sum modulo 10000. The final output should be the result of the modulo operation.
