Design a system that combines the two given modules: an 8-bit binary number storage module and a dual-edge triggered flip-flop module. The binary number storage module should be able to store 8-bit binary numbers and perform bit-wise logical operations on them. The dual-edge triggered flip-flop module should function like a dual-edge triggered flip-flop using only positive edge-triggered flip-flops and combinational logic, triggered on both edges of the clock. The system should also include an additional functional module that takes in the outputs of both modules and performs a bit-wise logical operation on them. The final output should be the result of the bit-wise logical operation.
Response:
module binary_storage (
    input clk,
    input reset,            // Synchronous reset
    input [7:0] d,
    input [2:0] op,         // Bit-wise logical operation to perform
    output reg [7:0] q
);

always @(posedge clk) begin
    if (reset) begin
        q <= 8'b0;
    end else begin
        case (op)
            3'b000: q <= d & q;   // AND
            3'b001: q <= d | q;   // OR
            3'b010: q <= d ^ q;   // XOR
            3'b011: q <= ~d;      // NOT
            3'b100: q <= d;       // Load
            default: q <= q;      // No operation
        endcase
    end
end

endmodule

module dual_edge_triggered_flip_flop (
    input clk,
    input reset,            // Synchronous reset
    input d,
    output reg q
);

reg q1, q2;

always @(posedge clk) begin
    if (reset) begin
        q1 <= 1'b0;
        q2 <= 1'b0;
    end else begin
        q1 <= d;
    end
end

always @(negedge clk) begin
    q2 <= q1;
end

assign q = q2;

endmodule

module bitwise_logic (
    input [7:0] a,
    input [7:0] b,
    input [2:0] op,         // Bit-wise logical operation to perform
    output reg [7:0] q
);

always @* begin
    case (op)
        3'b000: q = a & b;   // AND
        3'b001: q = a | b;   // OR
        3'b010: q = a ^ b;   // XOR
        3'b011: q = ~a;      // NOT
        default: q = 8'b0;    // No operation
    endcase
end

endmodule

module top_module (
    input clk,
    input reset,            // Synchronous reset
    input [7:0] d,
    input select,           // Select input to choose between modules
    output q
);

reg [7:0] binary_storage_q;
reg dual_edge_triggered_flip_flop_q;
reg [7:0] bitwise_logic_q;

binary_storage binary_storage_inst (
    .clk(clk),
    .reset(reset),
    .d(d),
    .op(select ? 3'b100 : 3'b111),   // Load if select is high, no operation otherwise
    .q(binary_storage_q)
);

dual_edge_triggered_flip_flop dual_edge_triggered_flip_flop_inst (
    .clk(clk),
    .reset(reset),
    .d(select),
    .q(dual_edge_triggered_flip_flop_q)
);

bitwise_logic bitwise_logic_inst (
    .a(binary_storage_q),
    .b(dual_edge_triggered_flip_flop_q),
    .op(3'b000),   // AND
    .q(bitwise_logic_q)
);

assign q = bitwise_logic_q;

endmodule

  input SET,

);

module binary_counter(
  input clk,        // clock input
  input reset,      // reset input
  input load,       // load input
  input [3:0] target,  // target value input
  output reg [3:0] count,  // binary count output
  output reg equal  // target value equality output
);

  always @(posedge clk) begin
    if (reset) begin
      count <= 4'b0000;
    end else if (load) begin
      count <= target;
    end else begin
      count <= count + 1;
    end
  end
  
  always @(*) begin
    if (count == target) begin
      equal = 1;
    end else begin
      equal = 0;
    end
  end

endmodule

- When the clock signal (clk) is asserted, the data_out signal should output the data item that was last written into the memory block.
- When the reset signal (rst) is asserted, the memory block should be cleared and the data_out signal should output 0.

To implement the LIFO memory block, you should use Verilog code to define a memory array and a pointer that keeps track of the last data item written into the memory block. 
You should also use a case statement to determine the behavior of the module based on the input signals. 
Finally, you should use the pointer to retrieve the last data item written into the memory block.

module lifo_memory (
  input clk,
  input wr_en,
  input [7:0] data_in,
  input rst,
  output [7:0] data_out
);

parameter depth = 8; // number of data items that can be stored in the memory block

reg [7:0] memory [0:depth-1]; // memory array
reg [2:0] pointer = 0; // pointer to last data item written into the memory block

always @(posedge clk) begin
  if (rst) begin
    pointer <= 0; // reset pointer
    data_out <= 0; // output 0
  end
  else begin
    case ({wr_en, pointer})
      2'b01: begin // write data_in to memory
        memory[pointer] <= data_in;
        pointer <= pointer + 1;
      end
      2'b10: begin // read last data item written to memory
        data_out <= memory[pointer-1];
        pointer <= pointer - 1;
      end
      default: data_out <= data_out; // do nothing
    endcase
  end
end

endmodule

module up_down_counter (
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input ena,
    input ld,
    input [3:0] data,
    output reg [3:0] q
);

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (rst) begin
            q <= 4'b0;
        end
        else if (ena) begin
            if (ld) begin
                q <= data;
            end
            else begin
                if (q == 4'b1111) begin
                    q <= 4'b0000;
                end
                else if (q == 4'b0000) begin
                    q <= 4'b1111;
                end
                else begin
                    if (ld) begin
                        q <= data;
                    end
                    else if (q < 4'b1111 && !ld) begin
                        q <= q + 1;
                    end
                    else if (q > 4'b0000 && !ld) begin
                        q <= q - 1;
                    end
                end
            end
        end
    end

endmodule

);

module shift_register (

  input LOAD,
  input [3:0] DATA_IN,

);

Outputs: a set of m output signals (out1, out2, ..., outm)

The IR transmitter should be able to transmit data using IR signals. The data to be transmitted should be provided as input to the module.
The IR receiver should be able to receive IR signals and convert them into digital signals. The received data should be output by the module.
The module should include a protocol for transmitting and receiving data using IR signals. This protocol should include a start bit, a data byte, and a stop bit.
The module should be able to operate at a specific frequency, which should be determined by the clock signal.

To implement the IR communication block, you should use Verilog code to define the protocol for transmitting and receiving data using IR signals. 
You should then use this protocol to connect the inputs to the IR transmitter and the IR receiver, and to convert the received signals into digital signals. 
Finally, you should use the digital signals to output the received data.

module IR_communication_block (
  input [n-1:0] in,
  input clk,
  output [m-1:0] out
);

parameter n = 8; // number of input signals (data to be transmitted)
parameter m = 8; // number of output signals (received data)

reg [n+1:0] tx_data; // data to be transmitted
reg [n+1:0] rx_data; // received data
reg tx_busy; // flag indicating if transmitter is busy
reg rx_busy; // flag indicating if receiver is busy
reg tx_done; // flag indicating if transmission is complete
reg rx_done; // flag indicating if reception is complete
reg [1:0] tx_state; // state of transmitter
reg [1:0] rx_state; // state of receiver
reg [7:0] tx_count; // counter for transmitting data
reg [7:0] rx_count; // counter for receiving data

// IR transmitter
always @(posedge clk) begin
  case (tx_state)
    2'b00: begin // idle state
      if (!tx_busy) begin
        tx_data[0] = 1'b0; // start bit
        tx_data[n+1] = 1'b1; // stop bit
        tx_count = 0;
        tx_state = 2'b01; // go to transmit state
      end
    end
    2'b01: begin // transmit state
      if (tx_count < n+2) begin
        out = tx_data[tx_count];
        tx_count = tx_count + 1;
      end else begin
        tx_busy = 1'b0;
        tx_done = 1'b1;
        tx_state = 2'b00; // go back to idle state
      end
    end
  endcase
end

// IR receiver
always @(posedge clk) begin
  case (rx_state)
    2'b00: begin // idle state
      if (in == 1'b0) begin
        rx_count = 0;
        rx_state = 2'b01; // go to receive state
      end
    end
    2'b01: begin // receive state
      if (rx_count < n+2) begin
        rx_data[rx_count] = in;
        rx_count = rx_count + 1;
      end else begin
        rx_busy = 1'b0;
        rx_done = 1'b1;
        rx_state = 2'b00; // go back to idle state
      end
    end
  endcase
end

// top-level module
always @(posedge clk) begin
  if (!tx_busy && !rx_busy) begin
    tx_busy = 1'b1;
    tx_done = 1'b0;
    tx_state = 2'b00;
    rx_busy = 1'b1;
    rx_done = 1'b0;
    rx_state = 2'b00;
  end
end

endmodule

module mem_protect (
  input [n-1:0] addr,
  input [m-1:0] ctrl,
  output mem_en
);

parameter n = 4; // number of address signals
parameter m = 2; // number of control signals
parameter memory_size = 1024; // size of the memory block to be protected.

always @(*) begin

  end
end

endmodule

module Pipeline_Register (
  input clk,
  input rst,
  input en,
  input [n-1:0] in,
  output [n-1:0] out
);

reg [n-1:0] reg_out; // register output

always @(posedge clk) begin
  if (rst) begin
    reg_out <= 0; // reset to all zeros

end

assign out = reg_out; // assign register output to output signals

endmodule

- The output `q` should be synchronous to the input `clk`
- When the reset signal `rst` is asserted, the output `q` should be set to 1

module d_flip_flop (
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input d,
    output reg q
);

always @(posedge clk, negedge rst) begin
    if (~rst) begin
        q <= 1;
    end else begin
        q <= ~d;
    end
end

endmodule

module counter_4bit (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input enable,
    output reg [3:0] Q
);

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            Q <= 4'b0000;
        end else if (enable) begin
            Q <= Q + 1;
        end
    end

endmodule

In the TRANSMIT state, the module should shift the data in the shift register out on the data_out signal, one bit at a time.
Once all the data bits have been transmitted, the module should transition back to the IDLE state.
The transmit enable signal (tx_en) and receive enable signal (rx_en) should be asserted when the module is in the TRANSMIT and RECEIVE states, respectively.
The data ready signal (data_ready) should be asserted when the module has received or transmitted data and is ready for the next operation.

module barrel_shifter (

    input [3:0] DATA,

);

- If `addr` is `2'b00`, `dout` should be equal to `{busy, 5'd0, flag_B, flag_A }`.
- If `addr` is `2'b01`, `dout` should be equal to `psg_dout` if the `use_ssg` parameter is set to 1, and `{busy, 5'd0, flag_B, flag_A }` otherwise.
- If `addr` is anything else, `dout` should be equal to `{busy, 5'd0, flag_B, flag_A }` if the `use_adpcm` parameter is not set to 1. If `use_adpcm` is set to 1, `dout` should be equal to `{ adpcmb_flag, 1'b0, adpcma_flags }`.

    input             clk,        // CPU clock
    input             flag_A,
    input             flag_B,
    input             busy,
    input      [5:0]  adpcma_flags,
    input             adpcmb_flag,
    input      [7:0]  psg_dout,
    input      [1:0]  addr,
    output reg [7:0]  dout
);

parameter use_ssg=0, use_adpcm=0;

always @(posedge clk) begin
    casez( addr )
        2'b00: dout <= {busy, 5'd0, flag_B, flag_A }; // YM2203
        2'b01: dout <= (use_ssg  ==1) ? psg_dout : {busy, 5'd0, flag_B, flag_A };
        2'b1?: dout <= (use_adpcm==1) ?
            { adpcmb_flag, 1'b0, adpcma_flags } :
            { busy, 5'd0, flag_B, flag_A };
    endcase
end

endmodule

module up_down_counter (
    input clk,
    input areset,
    input load,
    input up_down,
    input count_enable,
    output reg [3:0] count_out
);

always @(posedge clk or negedge areset) begin
    if (areset == 0) begin
        count_out <= 4'b0000;
    end else if (load == 1) begin
        count_out <= add_sub_out;
    end else if (count_enable == 1) begin
        if (up_down == 1) begin
            count_out <= count_out + 1;
        end else begin
            count_out <= count_out - 1;
        end
    end
end

endmodule

module adder_subtractor (
    input [3:0] in1,
    input [3:0] in2,
    input sub,
    output reg [3:0] out
);

always @(*) begin
    if (sub == 1) begin
        out = in1 - in2;
    end else begin
        out = in1 + in2;
    end
end

endmodule

module functional_module (
    input [3:0] count_out,
    input [3:0] add_sub_out,
    input count_enable,
    output reg [3:0] final_output,
    output reg max_reached
);

always @(count_out, add_sub_out, count_enable) begin
    if (count_enable == 1) begin
        final_output <= add_sub_out;
        if (count_out == 4'b1111 && add_sub_out == 4'b1111) begin
            max_reached <= 1;
        end else if (count_out == 4'b0000 && add_sub_out == 4'b0000) begin
            max_reached <= 1;
        end else begin
            max_reached <= 0;
        end
    end else begin
        final_output <= 4'b0000;
        max_reached <= 0;
    end
end

endmodule

module top_module (
    input clk,
    input areset,
    input load,
    input up_down,
    input count_enable,
    input [3:0] add_sub_in,
    input sub,
    output [3:0] final_output,
    output max_reached
);

wire [3:0] add_sub_out;

- an enable signal (en)
- a reset signal (rst)
Outputs: 
- a timeout signal (timeout)

The module should also have the following parameters:
- t: the timeout interval in clock cycles

Your module should implement the following functionality:
- The timer should start counting when the enable signal goes high.
- If the timer reaches the timeout interval, it should set the timeout signal to high.
- If the reset signal goes high, the timer should reset to zero.
- If the enable signal goes low, the timer should pause counting.

To implement the watchdog timer, you should use Verilog code to count the number of clock cycles that have elapsed since the enable signal went high. You should use a counter to keep track of the elapsed time, and you should compare the counter value to the timeout interval to determine if the timeout signal should be set. You should also use the reset signal to reset the counter to zero and use the enable signal to control whether the counter is counting or paused.

module WatchdogTimer (
  input clk,
  input en,
  input rst,
  output timeout
);

  parameter t = 100; // timeout interval in clock cycles.

  reg [7:0] counter; // 8-bit counter to keep track of elapsed time
  reg counting; // flag to control whether the counter is counting or paused

  always @(posedge clk) begin
    if (rst) begin
      counter <= 0;
      counting <= 0;
    end
    else if (en) begin
      counting <= 1;
      if (counting && (counter < t)) begin
        counter <= counter + 1;
      end
      else begin
        timeout <= 1;
      end
    end
    else begin
      counting <= 0;
    end
  end

endmodule

module rotator(
    input clk,
    input load,
    input [1:0] ena,
    input [99:0] data,
    output reg [99:0] q);

    reg [99:0] shift_reg;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (load) begin
            shift_reg <= data;

            case (ena)
                2'b00: shift_reg <= {shift_reg[98:0], shift_reg[99]};

Please act as a professional Verilog designer. Your task is to create a Verilog module that implements a debouncer. 
A debouncer is a digital circuit that removes noise or glitches from a signal by delaying the output for a certain amount of time. 
The input signal is typically a button or a switch that can generate multiple pulses when pressed or released.
Your module should have the following inputs and outputs:

Inputs: a single input signal (in)
Outputs: a single output signal (out)

Your module should implement the following functionality:
The circuit should generate a single pulse for each press or release of the input signal.
The circuit should remove any glitches or noise from the input signal.
The circuit should have a configurable delay to prevent multiple pulses from being generated.

To implement the debouncer, you should use Verilog code to define a simple state machine that detects the rising and falling edges of the input signal. 
You should then use a delay element to generate a single pulse for each edge. 
The delay element should have a configurable delay to prevent multiple pulses from being generated for a single edge. 
Finally, you should use the output of the delay element to generate the output signal.
Response:
module Debouncer (
  input in,
  output out
);

  parameter DELAY = 10; // configurable delay in clock cycles
  
  reg [1:0] state = 2'b00; // state machine
  
  reg out_reg = 1'b0; // output register
  wire in_sync = in & ~out_reg; // synchronized input signal
  
  always @(posedge clk) begin
    case(state)
      2'b00: begin // idle state
        if (in_sync) begin
          state <= 2'b01; // transition to state 1
        end
      end
      2'b01: begin // delay state
        if (in_sync) begin
          state <= 2'b01; // stay in state 1
        end else begin
          state <= 2'b10; // transition to state 2
        end
      end
      2'b10: begin // debounce state
        if (in_sync) begin
          state <= 2'b10; // stay in state 2
        end else begin
          state <= 2'b00; // transition to state 0
        end
      end
    endcase
  end
  
  always @(posedge clk) begin
    case(state)
      2'b00: begin // idle state
        out_reg <= 1'b0;
      end
      2'b01: begin // delay state
        #DELAY out_reg <= 1'b1; // generate pulse after delay
      end
      2'b10: begin // debounce state
        out_reg <= 1'b0;
      end
    endcase
  end
  
  assign out = out_reg;
  
endmodule

The reset should be triggered by an additional functional module that takes the output of the 8th D flip-flop as input. The D flip-flops should count from 0 to 7, and the output should be the count value. Use the positive edge of the clock to trigger the flip-flops.

module counter (
    input clk,         // Clock input
    input reset,       // Asynchronous active-high reset
    output reg [2:0] q // 3-bit output from the counter
);

    reg [2:0] next_q;   // Next state of the counter

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            q <= 3'b000; // Reset the counter to 0
        end else begin
            q <= next_q; // Update the counter with the next state
        end
    end

    // Compute the next state of the counter
    always @* begin
        if (q == 3'b111) begin
            next_q = 3'b000; // Reset the counter to 0
        end else begin
            next_q = q + 1;  // Increment the counter
        end
    end

endmodule

module reset_trigger (
    input reset_trigger, // Input from the 8th D flip-flop
    output reset        // Output to the counter reset
);

    assign reset = reset_trigger;

endmodule

module top_module (
    input clk,         // Clock input
    input reset,       // Asynchronous active-high reset
    output [2:0] q     // 3-bit output from the counter
);

    wire reset_trigger; // Output from the 8th D flip-flop

    // Instantiate the counter and reset_trigger modules
    counter counter_inst (
        .clk(clk),
        .reset(reset_trigger),
        .q(q)
    );

    reset_trigger reset_trigger_inst (
        .reset_trigger(q[2]), // Use the output of the 8th D flip-flop as input
        .reset(reset)
    );

    // Instantiate 8 D flip-flops
    reg [7:0] d_ff;
    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            d_ff <= 8'b00000000; // Reset the D flip-flops to 0
        end else begin
            d_ff <= {d_ff[6:0], q[2]}; // Shift the output of the 7th D flip-flop to the 8th D flip-flop
        end
    end

endmodule

When the counter reaches the maximum count value, it should stop incrementing and keep outputting the same value until the `reset` signal is asserted.

Response:
module counter (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input enable,
    input [31:0] max_count,
    output reg [31:0] out
);

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (reset) begin
            out <= 0;
        end else if (enable) begin
            if (out == max_count) begin
                out <= out;
            end else begin
                out <= out + 1;
            end
        end
    end

endmodule

  // parameters

  parameter   SINGLE_ENDED = 0,
  parameter   DEVICE_TYPE = 0,
  parameter   IODELAY_ENABLE = 1,
  parameter   IODELAY_CTRL = 0,
  parameter   IODELAY_GROUP = "dev_if_delay_group") (

  // data interface

  input               rx_clk,
  input               rx_data_in_p,
  input               rx_data_in_n,
  output              rx_data_p,
  output              rx_data_n,

  // delay-data interface

  input               up_clk,
  input               up_dld,
  input       [ 4:0]  up_dwdata,
  output      [ 4:0]  up_drdata,

  // delay-cntrl interface

  input               delay_clk,
  input               delay_rst,
  output              delay_locked);

  // internal parameters

  localparam  NONE = -1;
  localparam  VIRTEX7 = 0;
  localparam  ULTRASCALE_PLUS = 2;
  localparam  ULTRASCALE = 3;

  localparam  IODELAY_CTRL_ENABLED = (IODELAY_ENABLE == 1) ? IODELAY_CTRL : 0;
  localparam  IODELAY_CTRL_SIM_DEVICE = (DEVICE_TYPE == ULTRASCALE_PLUS) ? "ULTRASCALE" :
    (DEVICE_TYPE == ULTRASCALE) ? "ULTRASCALE" : "7SERIES";

  localparam  IODELAY_DEVICE_TYPE = (IODELAY_ENABLE == 1) ? DEVICE_TYPE : NONE;
  localparam  IODELAY_SIM_DEVICE = (DEVICE_TYPE == ULTRASCALE_PLUS) ? "ULTRASCALE_PLUS" :
    (DEVICE_TYPE == ULTRASCALE) ? "ULTRASCALE" : "7SERIES";

  // internal signals

  wire                rx_data_ibuf_s;
  wire                rx_data_idelay_s;
  wire        [ 8:0]  up_drdata_s;

  // delay controller

  generate
  if (IODELAY_CTRL_ENABLED == 0) begin
  assign delay_locked = 1'b1;
  end else begin
  (* IODELAY_GROUP = IODELAY_GROUP *)
  IDELAYCTRL #(.SIM_DEVICE (IODELAY_CTRL_SIM_DEVICE)) i_delay_ctrl (
    .RST (delay_rst),
    .REFCLK (delay_clk),
    .RDY (delay_locked));
  end
  endgenerate

  // receive data interface, ibuf -> idelay -> iddr

  generate
  if (SINGLE_ENDED == 1) begin
  IBUF i_rx_data_ibuf (

   b. When currentState is green, nextState should be yellow after 5 clock cycles.
   c. When currentState is yellow, nextState should be red after 2 clock cycles.
3. The traffic light controller should reset to the red state after a power-on reset.

  input clk,
  input [1:0] currentState,
  output reg [1:0] nextState
);

initial begin
  nextState <= 2'b00; // Red state
end

// Define state transitions
always @(posedge clk) begin
  case (currentState)
    2'b00: // Red state
      if (count == 10) begin
        nextState <= 2'b10; // Green state
        count <= 0;
      end else begin
        count <= count + 1;
      end
    2'b10: // Green state
      if (count == 5) begin
        nextState <= 2'b01; // Yellow state
        count <= 0;
      end else begin
        count <= count + 1;
      end
    2'b01: // Yellow state
      if (count == 2) begin
        nextState <= 2'b00; // Red state
        count <= 0;
      end else begin
        count <= count + 1;
      end
    default: nextState <= 2'b00; // Red state
  endcase
end

reg [2:0] count;
parameter CLK_PERIOD = 10; // Clock period in ns
always #CLK_PERIOD clk = ~clk; // Toggle clock signal

    input [3:0] B,
    input [2:0] op,

);

    end

endmodule

A LIFO memory block is a type of digital circuit that stores and retrieves data in a last-in-first-out order. 
The circuit should have a set of data inputs and a set of data outputs. 
When data is written into the memory block, it is stored in a stack. 
The last data that was written into the stack is the first data that is read out of the stack.

Your module should have the following inputs and outputs:

Inputs: 
- data_in: the data to be written into the memory block (n-bit wide)
- write_en: a write enable signal
- read_en: a read enable signal

Outputs: 
- data_out: the data that is read from the memory block (n-bit wide)

The module should also have the following parameters:

- n: the width of the data bus
- depth: the depth of the memory block (i.e., the number of data elements that can be stored in the memory block)

Your module should implement the following functionality:

- When write_en is high, the data_in should be written into the memory block.
- When read_en is high, the last data that was written into the memory block should be read out of the memory block and output on the data_out bus.
- If there is no data in the memory block, the data_out bus should output zeros.

To implement the LIFO memory block, you should use Verilog code to define a stack data structure that stores the data elements. 
You should then use this stack to write and read data from the memory block as described above. 
Note that the stack should have a size of "depth", which is a parameter defined in your module.

module lifo_memory (
  input [n-1:0] data_in,
  input write_en,
  input read_en,
  output [n-1:0] data_out
);

parameter n = 8;    // width of the data bus
parameter depth = 16;  // depth of the memory block

reg [n-1:0] memory [0:depth-1];  // stack data structure to store the data elements
reg [4:0] top = 0;  // variable to keep track of the top of the stack

always @ (posedge clk) begin
  if (write_en) begin
    memory[top] <= data_in;  // write data_in to the top of the stack
    top <= top + 1;  // increment the top of the stack
  end
  else if (read_en) begin
    if (top > 0) begin
      top <= top - 1;  // decrement the top of the stack
      data_out <= memory[top];  // read the data from the top of the stack
    end
    else begin
      data_out <= 0;  // if there is no data in the stack, output zeros
    end
  end
end

endmodule

- Read data from memory at the given address
- Update data in memory at the given address

Your task is to implement the RAM module in Verilog within 200 lines of code.

module RAM (
    // OUTPUTs
    output reg [15:0] ram_douta, // RAM data output (Port A)
    output reg [15:0] ram_doutb, // RAM data output (Port B)

    // INPUTs
    input [6:0] ram_addra, // RAM address (Port A)
    input ram_cena, // RAM chip enable (low active) (Port A)
    input ram_clka, // RAM clock (Port A)
    input [15:0] ram_dina, // RAM data input (Port A)
    input [1:0] ram_wena, // RAM write enable (low active) (Port A)
    input [6:0] ram_addrb, // RAM address (Port B)
    input ram_cenb, // RAM chip enable (low active) (Port B)
    input ram_clkb, // RAM clock (Port B)
    input [15:0] ram_dinb, // RAM data input (Port B)
    input [1:0] ram_wenb // RAM write enable (low active) (Port B)
);

    // PARAMETERs
    parameter ADDR_MSB = 6; // MSB of the address bus
    parameter MEM_SIZE = 256; // Memory size in bytes

    // RAM
    reg [15:0] mem [0:(MEM_SIZE/2)-1]; // 16-bit memory array
    reg [6:0] addr_reg_a, addr_reg_b; // address registers for Port A and Port B

    // Port A
    always @(posedge ram_clka) begin
        if (!ram_cena && ram_addra <= (MEM_SIZE/2)-1) begin
            case (ram_wena)
                2'b00: mem[ram_addra] <= ram_dina; // write data to memory
                2'b01: mem[ram_addra] <= {ram_dina[15:8], mem[ram_addra][7:0]}; // update upper byte of data
                2'b10: mem[ram_addra] <= {mem[ram_addra][15:8], ram_dina[7:0]}; // update lower byte of data
            endcase
            addr_reg_a <= ram_addra; // store address in register
        end
    end
    assign ram_douta = mem[addr_reg_a]; // read data from memory

    // Port B
    always @(posedge ram_clkb) begin
        if (!ram_cenb && ram_addrb <= (MEM_SIZE/2)-1) begin
            case (ram_wenb)
                2'b00: mem[ram_addrb] <= ram_dinb; // write data to memory
                2'b01: mem[ram_addrb] <= {ram_dinb[15:8], mem[ram_addrb][7:0]}; // update upper byte of data
                2'b10: mem[ram_addrb] <= {mem[ram_addrb][15:8], ram_dinb[7:0]}; // update lower byte of data
            endcase
            addr_reg_b <= ram_addrb; // store address in register
        end
    end
    assign ram_doutb = mem[addr_reg_b]; // read data from memory

endmodule

Please act as a professional Verilog designer. Your task is to create a Verilog module that implements a multi-port RAM block. 
A multi-port RAM block is a type of digital circuit that provides multiple read and write ports to access a shared memory array. 
The inputs to the circuit are the address and data signals for each port, and the outputs are the data signals read from the memory array for each port. 
Your module should have the following inputs and outputs:

Inputs: a set of n address signals (addr1, addr2, ..., addrn) and a set of m data signals (data1, data2, ..., datam) for each port
Outputs: a set of m data signals (out1, out2, ..., outm) for each port
The module should also have the following parameters:

n: the number of address signals for each port
m: the number of data signals for each port
k: the number of ports
w: the width of each data signal in bits
Your module should implement the following functionality:

The circuit should have a shared memory array with a capacity of 2^w words, each of which is w bits wide.
The circuit should have k read ports and k write ports, each with n address signals and m data signals.
Each read port should be able to read any word from the memory array, and each write port should be able to write any word to the memory array.
If multiple ports try to access the same word at the same time, the circuit should resolve the conflicts using a predefined arbitration policy, such as round-robin or priority-based.
To implement the multi-port RAM block, you should use Verilog code to define the memory array and the arbitration policy for accessing the memory array. 
You should then use these functions to connect the input and output ports to the memory array, and ensure that the memory array is accessed in a synchronized manner.
Finally, you should use the arbitration policy to resolve any conflicts between the read and write ports that occur concurrently.
Response:
module multiport_ram #(
  parameter n = 8, // number of address signals for each port
  parameter m = 32, // number of data signals for each port
  parameter k = 4, // number of ports
  parameter w = 8 // width of each data signal in bits
) (
  input [n-1:0] addr[k-1:0],
  input [m-1:0] data[k-1:0],
  output [m-1:0] out[k-1:0]
);

  reg [w-1:0] mem [0:(1<<n)-1]; // memory array
  integer i, j;

  // Arbitration policy: round-robin
  always @(*) begin
    for (i = 0; i < k; i = i + 1) begin
      out[i] = mem[addr[i]];
    end
  end

  // Write to memory
  always @(posedge clk) begin
    for (i = 0; i < k; i = i + 1) begin
      for (j = 0; j < k; j = j + 1) begin
        if (i != j) begin
          if (addr[i] != addr[j]) begin
            mem[addr[i]] <= data[i];
          end
        end
      end
    end
  end

endmodule

The inputs to the circuit are the step and direction signals, and the output is the control signal for the stepper motor.

Outputs: control signal for the stepper motor (ctrl)

Your module should implement the following functionality:

The circuit should generate a pulse train on the control signal for the stepper motor. 
The pulse train should have a frequency that corresponds to the desired speed of the stepper motor, and the number of pulses per revolution should be equal to steps_per_rev.
The circuit should also change the direction of the stepper motor depending on the value of the direction signal.
To implement the motor control block, you should use Verilog code to generate a pulse train on the control signal for the stepper motor. 
You should use the step signal to control the timing of the pulse train, and the direction signal to change the direction of the stepper motor. 
To generate the pulse train, you should use a counter and a comparator to determine when to generate a pulse. 
You should then use a flip-flop to store the direction of the stepper motor.

module motor_control (
  input step,
  input dir,
  output ctrl
);

  parameter steps_per_rev = 200; // number of steps per revolution
  
  reg [7:0] count = 0; // 8-bit counter for pulse generation
  reg direction = 1; // flip-flop to store direction of stepper motor
  
  always @(posedge step) begin
    if (count == steps_per_rev) begin
      count <= 0;
    end else begin
      count <= count + 1;
    end
  end
  
  always @(posedge step) begin
    if (dir == 1) begin
      direction <= ~direction;
    end
  end
  
  assign ctrl = (count == steps_per_rev/2) ? direction : ~direction; // generate pulse train
  
endmodule

Please act as a professional Verilog designer. Create a system that utilizes a barrel shifter and a multiplexer to implement an 8-bit shifter and adder. The system should include a module that combines a rotator module and an adder module. The rotator module should be able to rotate the stored data by 2 bits to the right or left, with synchronous load and enable. The adder module should perform an addition between two 8-bit inputs. The combined system should also include an additional control logic module that enables either the rotator module or the adder module based on a select input. The output should be the active module's value.

module rotator (
  input clk,
  input reset, // Synchronous active-high reset
  input [7:0] data_in, // 8-bit input data
  input [1:0] shift_dir, // Direction of shift (0: right, 1: left)
  input load, // Synchronous load input
  input [1:0] ena, // Synchronous enable input
  output reg [7:0] data_out // 8-bit output data
);

  always @(posedge clk, posedge reset) begin
    if (reset) begin
      data_out <= 8'b0;
    end else if (load) begin
      data_out <= data_in;
    end else if (ena[0]) begin
      if (shift_dir[0]) begin
        data_out <= {data_out[6:0], data_out[7]};
      end else begin
        data_out <= {data_out[0], data_out[7:1]};
      end
    end else if (ena[1]) begin
      if (shift_dir[1]) begin
        data_out <= {data_out[4:0], data_out[7:5]};
      end else begin
        data_out <= {data_out[2:7], data_out[1:0]};
      end
    end
  end

endmodule

module adder (
  input [7:0] a, // 8-bit input for the first operand
  input [7:0] b, // 8-bit input for the second operand
  output reg [7:0] q // 8-bit output for the sum
);

  always @(a, b) begin
    q <= a + b;
  end

endmodule

module top_module (
  input clk,
  input reset, // Synchronous active-high reset
  input [7:0] a, // 8-bit input for the first operand of the adder module
  input [7:0] b, // 8-bit input for the second operand of the adder module
  input load, // Synchronous load input for the rotator module
  input [1:0] ena, // Synchronous enable input for the rotator module
  input select, // Select input to choose between rotator module or adder module
  output [7:0] q // 8-bit output from the active module
);

  wire [7:0] rotator_out;
  wire [7:0] adder_out;

  rotator rotator_inst (
    .clk(clk),
    .reset(reset),
    .data_in(select ? rotator_out : a),
    .shift_dir(ena),
    .load(load),
    .ena(ena),
    .data_out(rotator_out)
  );

  adder adder_inst (
    .a(a),
    .b(b),
    .q(adder_out)
  );

  mux2to1 #(.WIDTH(8)) mux_inst (
    .a(rotator_out),
    .b(adder_out),
    .sel(select),
    .out(q)
  );

endmodule

module mux2to1 #(parameter WIDTH=8) (
  input [WIDTH-1:0] a,
  input [WIDTH-1:0] b,
  input sel,
  output reg [WIDTH-1:0] out
);

  always @(a, b, sel) begin
    if (sel) begin
      out <= b;
    end else begin
      out <= a;
    end
  end

endmodule

  input clk,
  input [7:0] duty_cycle, // 8-bit duty cycle input (0-255)
  output pwm_out
);

  reg pwm_out_reg = 0; // PWM output register

    counter <= counter + 1; // Increment the counter on every clock cycle
    if (counter >= 255) begin

module shift_register (
  input clk,      // clock input
  input load,     // load input
  input control,  // control input
  input [7:0] data_in,  // input data
  output [7:0] data_out // output data
);

  reg [7:0] register;  // shift register

  always @ (posedge clk) begin
    if (load) begin  // if load is high, load the input data
      register <= data_in;
    end else begin  // otherwise, shift the data based on the control input
      if (control) begin  // shift left
        register <= {register[6:0], register[7]};
      end else begin  // shift right
        register <= {register[0], register[7:1]};
      end
    end
  end

  assign data_out = register;  // output the data in the shift register

endmodule

module oh_pads_domain #(parameter TYPE = "SOFT",
                        parameter DIR = "NO",
                        parameter NGPIO = 8,
                        parameter NVDDIO = 8,
                        parameter NVSSIO = 8,
                        parameter NVDD = 8,
                        parameter NVSS = 8,
                        parameter POC = 1,
                        parameter LEFTCUT = 1,
                        parameter RIGHTCUT = 1)
                       (inout [NGPIO-1:0] pad,
                        inout vddio,
                        inout vssio,
                        inout vdd,
                        inout vss,
                        inout poc,
                        input [NGPIO-1:0] dout,
                        output [NGPIO-1:0] din,
                        input [NGPIO-1:0] oen,
                        input [NGPIO-1:0] ie,
                        input [NGPIO*8-1:0] cfg);

   generate
      genvar i;

      // IO BUFFERS
      for (i = 0; i < NGPIO; i = i + 1) begin : padio
         asic_iobuf #(.DIR(DIR), .TYPE(TYPE)) i0 (.din(din[i]), .dout(dout[i]),
                                                   .ie(ie[i]), .oen(oen[i]),
                                                   .cfg(cfg[i*8+:8]),
                                                   .poc(poc), .vdd(vdd), .vss(vss),
                                                   .vddio(vddio), .vssio(vssio),
                                                   .pad(pad[i]));
      end

      // IO SUPPLY PINS
      for (i = 0; i < NVDDIO; i = i + 1) begin : padvddio
         asic_iovddio #(.DIR(DIR), .TYPE(TYPE)) i0 (.vdd(vdd), .vss(vss),
                                                   .vddio(vddio), .vssio(vssio),
                                                   .poc(poc));
      end

      // IO GROUND PINS
      for (i = 0; i < NVSSIO; i = i + 1) begin : padvssio
         asic_iovssio #(.DIR(DIR), .TYPE(TYPE)) i0 (.vdd(vdd), .vss(vss),
                                                   .vddio(vddio), .vssio(vssio),
                                                   .poc(poc));
      end

      // CORE SUPPLY PINS
      for (i = 0; i < NVDD; i = i + 1) begin : padvdd
         asic_iovdd #(.DIR(DIR), .TYPE(TYPE)) i0 (.vdd(vdd), .vss(vss),
                                                 .vddio(vddio), .vssio(vssio),
                                                 .poc(poc));
      end

      // CORE GROUND PINS
      for (i = 0; i < NVSS; i = i + 1) begin : padvss
         asic_iovss #(.DIR(DIR), .TYPE(TYPE)) i0 (.vdd(vdd), .vss(vss),
                                                 .vddio(vddio), .vssio(vssio),
                                                 .poc(poc));
      end

      // CUT CELLS
      if (LEFTCUT == 1) begin : padcutleft
         asic_iocut #(.DIR(DIR), .TYPE(TYPE)) i0 (.vdd(vdd), .vss(vss),
                                                 .vddio(vddio), .vssio(vssio),
                                                 .poc(poc));
      end

      if (RIGHTCUT == 1) begin : padcutright
         asic_iocut #(.DIR(DIR), .TYPE(TYPE)) i0 (.vdd(vdd), .vss(vss),
                                                 .vddio(vddio), .vssio(vssio),
                                                 .poc(poc));
      end

      // POWER ON CONTROL
      if (POC == 1) begin : padpoc
         asic_iopoc #(.DIR(DIR), .TYPE(TYPE)) i0 (.vdd(vdd), .vss(vss),
                                                 .vddio(vddio), .vssio(vssio),
                                                 .poc(poc));
      end

   endgenerate

endmodule

module vga_memory(
  input clk,
  input reset,
  input [18:0] address,
  input [1:0] data_in,
  input write_enable,
  output reg [1:0] data_out
);

  reg [1:0] memory [0:307199]; // 640x480 pixels = 307200, but we index from 0

    end

    end

  end

endmodule

    input UP,
    input DOWN,
    input LOAD,
    input [3:0] DIN,
    output reg [3:0] Q
);

        end else if (UP) begin

endmodule

  input reset,
  input control,
  output reg [3:0] count
);

  input wire [width-1:0] data_in,

Please act as a professional Verilog designer. Your task is to create a Verilog module that implements a register file. 
A register file is a type of digital circuit that stores data values in a set of registers. The circuit can read data from one or more registers and write data to one or more registers at the same time.
Your module should have the following inputs and outputs:

Inputs: 
- clk: clock signal
- wr_en: write enable signal
- rd_en: read enable signal
- addr1: address of the first register
- addr2: address of the second register (optional)
- data_in: data to be written to the register(s)

Outputs:
- data_out1: data read from the first register
- data_out2: data read from the second register (optional)

The module should also have the following parameters:

n: the number of registers in the file
w: the width of each register (i.e., the number of bits in each register)

Your module should implement the following functionality:

- The circuit should have n registers, each of which is w bits wide.
- The circuit should be able to read data from one or more registers at the same time.
- The circuit should be able to write data to one or more registers at the same time.
- The circuit should only write data to the register(s) when the write enable signal is set.
- The circuit should only read data from the register(s) when the read enable signal is set.
- The circuit should read the data from the register(s) at the rising edge of the clock signal.

To implement the register file, you should use Verilog code to define the registers as an array of w-bit registers. 
You should use the address signals to select the registers to be read from or written to. 
You should use the write enable signal and data input to write data to the selected registers. 
Finally, you should use the read enable signal to read data from the selected registers and output it to the data output signals.
Response:
module register_file (
  input clk,
  input wr_en,
  input rd_en,
  input [log2(n)-1:0] addr1,
  input [log2(n)-1:0] addr2,
  input [w-1:0] data_in,
  output reg [w-1:0] data_out1,
  output reg [w-1:0] data_out2
);

parameter n = 8; // number of registers
parameter w = 8; // width of each register (in bits)
 
reg [w-1:0] registers [0:n-1]; // array of registers

always @(posedge clk) begin
  if (rd_en) begin
    data_out1 <= registers[addr1];
    if (addr2 != 0) data_out2 <= registers[addr2];
  end
  if (wr_en) begin
    registers[addr1] <= data_in;
    if (addr2 != 0) registers[addr2] <= data_in;
  end
end

endmodule

module clock_gate (
  input clk,
  input en,
  input te,
  output reg en_clk
);

  always @(posedge clk) begin
    if (en && te) begin

module tdpram #(
    parameter depth = 8, // depth of the memory (in bytes)
    parameter width = 8 // width of each memory element (in bits)
) (
    input sys_clk, // system clock
    
    input [depth-1:0] a, // address input
    input we, // write-enable signal
    input [width-1:0] di, // write data
    output reg [width-1:0] do // read data
);

reg [width-1:0] mem [0:(1<<depth)-1]; // memory array

always @(posedge sys_clk) begin
    if (we) begin
        mem[a] <= di; // write data to memory
    end
    do <= mem[a]; // read data from memory
end

endmodule


module twod_array_mem #(
    parameter depth = 256, // depth of the memory (in bytes)
    parameter width = 256 // width of each memory element (in bits)
) (
    input sys_clk, // system clock
    
    input we, // write-enable signal
    input [15:0] ra, // read address (16-bit aligned)
    input [15:0] wa, // write address (16-bit aligned)
    input [255:0] wd, // write data
    output reg [255:0] rd // read data
);

wire [7:0] rba = wa[7:0];

    .depth(depth/2),
    .width(width/2)
) ram0 (
    .sys_clk(sys_clk),
    .a({rab, raa}),
    .we(we),
    .di(wd[127:0]),

module binary_counter(
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire test_mode,
    input wire up,
    input wire down,
    output reg [3:0] count
);

    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst) begin
        if (~rst) begin
            count <= 4'b0;
        end else if (~test_mode) begin
            count <= count + 1;
        end else begin
            if (up) begin
                count <= (count == 4'b1111) ? 4'b0 : count + 1;
            end else if (down) begin
                count <= (count == 4'b0000) ? 4'b1111 : count - 1;
            end
        end
    end

endmodule

module up_down_counter (
    input clk,
    input load,
    input up_down,
    output reg [2:0] out
);

        if (load) begin
            out <= $random;
        end
        else if (up_down) begin
            out <= out + 1;
        end
        else begin
            out <= out - 1;

module adder_subtractor (

	input [3:0] B,
	input subtract,
	output reg [3:0] result
);

There are several types of flip-flops, including D flip-flops, JK flip-flops, T flip-flops, and SR flip-flops. 
Your module should be able to implement all four types of flip-flops.

Your module should have the following inputs and outputs:

Inputs:
- clk: a clock signal
- reset: a reset signal (active low)
- d: a data input signal
- j: a J input signal (for JK flip-flops)
- k: a K input signal (for JK flip-flops)
- t: a T input signal (for T flip-flops)
- s: an S input signal (for SR flip-flops)
- r: a R input signal (for SR flip-flops)

Outputs:
- q: the output signal
- qn: the complement of the output signal

To implement the flip-flops, you should use Verilog code to define the behavior of each type of flip-flop. 
You should then use these definitions to create a module that can implement any type of flip-flop based on the input signals.

For D flip-flops, the output is equal to the input when the clock signal transitions from low to high.
For JK flip-flops, the output is equal to the complement of the output when J and K are both high and the clock signal transitions from low to high.
For T flip-flops, the output toggles when the T input is high and the clock signal transitions from low to high.
For SR flip-flops, the output is set to the value of the S input when S is high and the clock signal transitions from low to high. The output is reset to the value of the R input when R is high and the clock signal transitions from low to high.
Response:
module flip_flop (
  input clk,
  input reset,
  input d,
  input j,
  input k,
  input t,
  input s,
  input r,
  output reg q,
  output reg qn
);

  always @(posedge clk, negedge reset) begin
    if (!reset) begin
      q <= 1'b0;
      qn <= 1'b1;
    end else begin
      case ({j,k,t,s,r})
        5'b00_0_: begin // D flip-flop
          q <= d;
        end
        5'b01_0_: begin // JK flip-flop
          q <= ~q;
        end
        5'b10_0_: begin // JK flip-flop
          q <= q;
        end
        5'b11_0_: begin // JK flip-flop
          q <= ~q;
        end
        5'b0_1_0: begin // T flip-flop
          q <= ~q;
        end
        5'b0_0_1: begin // SR flip-flop
          q <= s;
        end
        5'b0_1_1: begin // SR flip-flop
          q <= r;
        end
      endcase
    end
  end

  assign qn = ~q;

endmodule

Please act as a professional Verilog designer. Design a pipelined module that implements a 4-bit ALU (arithmetic logic unit). 
The module should take in two 4-bit inputs 'a' and 'b', and a 3-bit control signal 'op', 
and output a 4-bit result based on the selected operation, which includes addition, subtraction, bitwise AND, bitwise OR, bitwise XOR, or shift left. 
Use pipeline structure to achieve this functionality.
Response:
module alu (
    input [3:0] a,
    input [3:0] b,
    input [2:0] op,
    output reg [3:0] out
);

reg [3:0] a_reg, b_reg, alu_out_reg;

always @(posedge clk) begin
    a_reg <= a;
    b_reg <= b;
    case(op)
        3'b000: alu_out_reg <= a_reg + b_reg; // addition
        3'b001: alu_out_reg <= a_reg - b_reg; // subtraction
        3'b010: alu_out_reg <= a_reg & b_reg; // bitwise AND
        3'b011: alu_out_reg <= a_reg | b_reg; // bitwise OR
        3'b100: alu_out_reg <= a_reg ^ b_reg; // bitwise XOR
        3'b101: alu_out_reg <= {a_reg[2:0], 1'b0}; // shift left
        default: alu_out_reg <= 4'b0;
    endcase
end

always @(posedge clk) begin
    out <= alu_out_reg;
end

endmodule

- linear_flash_ce_n: output signal that is used to enable the chip select of the Linear Flash memory device.
- linear_flash_dq_io: 16-bit inout signal that is used to transfer data to and from the Linear Flash memory device.
- linear_flash_oen: output signal that is used to enable the output buffer of the Linear Flash memory device.
- linear_flash_wen: output signal that is used to enable the write enable of the Linear Flash memory device.

Your sub-module should be named "linear_flash" and should have the following inputs and outputs:

- clk: input clock signal.
- rst_n: input reset signal.
- addr: input 27-bit address signal.
- ce_n: input chip select signal.
- oe_n: input output enable signal.
- we_n: input write enable signal.
- dq_i: input 16-bit data signal for write operation.
- dq_o: output 16-bit data signal for read operation.

Your sub-module should implement the following functionality:

- The sub-module should be able to read and write data to the Linear Flash memory device using the provided signals.
- The sub-module should support byte-wide reads and writes to the Linear Flash memory device.
- The sub-module should implement the necessary timing constraints for interfacing with the Linear Flash memory device.
Response:
module linear_flash (
  input clk,
  input rst_n,
  input [26:0] addr,
  input ce_n,
  input oe_n,
  input we_n,
  input [15:0] dq_i,
  output [15:0] dq_o
);

  reg [15:0] memory [0:2**18-1];
  reg [15:0] data_out;

  always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
    if (!rst_n) begin
      data_out <= 16'h0;
    end
    else begin
      if (~ce_n) begin
        if (~oe_n && ~we_n) begin // read operation
          data_out <= memory[addr];
        end
        else if (~oe_n && we_n) begin // write operation
          memory[addr] <= dq_i;
        end
      end
    end
  end

  assign dq_o = data_out;

endmodule

Outputs:

The module should also have the following parameters:

- When the write enable signal is high, the data_in signal should be written to the memory location specified by the address signal.
- When the write enable signal is low, the data_out signal should output the data stored at the memory location specified by the address signal.

To implement the scratchpad memory block, you should use Verilog code to define an array that stores the data. The array should be indexed by the address signal to read/write data from/to the memory locations.
You should also use an if statement to check the write enable signal and perform the write operation when it is high. Finally, you should use another if statement to select the data to output based on the address signal when the write enable signal is low.

module Scratchpad (
  input clk,
  input we,
  input [addr_width-1:0] addr,
  input [data_width-1:0] data_in,
  output reg [data_width-1:0] data_out
);

parameter data_width = 8; // width of the data bus in bits
parameter addr_width = 6; // width of the address bus in bits
parameter depth = 64; // depth of the memory block in number of locations

reg [data_width-1:0] mem [0:depth-1]; // memory array

// write operation
always @(posedge clk) begin
  if (we) begin
    mem[addr] <= data_in;
  end
end

// read operation
always @(posedge clk) begin
  if (!we) begin
    data_out <= mem[addr];
  end
end

endmodule

module ClockPhaseShift(
  input wire clock,
  input wire reset,
  output reg locked,
  output reg clock_o0,
  output reg clock_o90,
  output reg clock_o180,
  output reg clock_o270,
  output reg clock_o2x,
  output reg clock_o2x180
);

  wire FPGABUFG_o;
  wire FPGASPDCM_CLK0;

  DCM_SP #(.CLKDV_DIVIDE(2.0), 
           .CLKFX_DIVIDE(1),
           .CLKFX_MULTIPLY(4),
           .CLKIN_DIVIDE_BY_2("FALSE"),
           .CLKIN_PERIOD(0.0),
           .CLKOUT_PHASE_SHIFT("NONE"),
           .CLK_FEEDBACK("1X"),
           .DESKEW_ADJUST("SYSTEM_SYNCHRONOUS"),
           .DLL_FREQUENCY_MODE("LOW"),
           .DUTY_CYCLE_CORRECTION("TRUE"),
           .PHASE_SHIFT(0),
           .STARTUP_WAIT("FALSE"))
  FPGASPDCM (.CLKIN(clock),
             .CLKFB(FPGABUFG_o),
             .RST(reset),
             .DSSEN(0),
             .PSINCDEC(0),
             .PSEN(0),
             .PSCLK(0),

             .LOCKED(locked),
             .CLK0(clock_o0),
             .CLK90(clock_o90),
             .CLK180(clock_o180),
             .CLK270(clock_o270),
             .CLK2X(clock_o2x),
             .CLK2X180(clock_o2x180));

  BUFG
  FPGABUFG (.I(FPGASPDCM_CLK0),
            .O(FPGABUFG_o));

endmodule

    input reset,   // Synchronous active-high reset
    output reg [3:1] ena,

        if (reset) begin
            q <= 16'h0000;
        end else begin
            if (ena[0]) begin
                q[3:0] <= q[3:0] + 1;
                if (q[3:0] == 10) begin
                    q[3:0] <= 4'h0;
                end

Please act as a professional Verilog designer. Your task is to create a Verilog module that implements thermal management blocks for temperature sensing and fan control. 
The module should have the following inputs and outputs:

1. A temperature sensor output signal, temp_sensor_out, which is a voltage signal that corresponds to the temperature of the device being monitored. 
2. A set of control signals (control1, control2, ...) that can be used to configure the thermal management blocks.

Outputs:
1. A fan control signal, fan_control, which is a voltage signal that controls the speed of a fan.
2. An alarm signal, alarm, which is a voltage signal that is set to high if the temperature exceeds a certain threshold.

The module should also have the following parameters:

n: the number of control signals

Your module should implement the following functionality:

1. The temperature sensor output signal, temp_sensor_out, should be converted into a temperature value using a linear equation. 
2. The temperature value should be compared to a threshold value, which is set using the control signals. If the temperature exceeds the threshold, the alarm signal should be set to high.
3. The fan control signal, fan_control, should be set based on the temperature value and the control signals. For example, you may want to increase the fan speed if the temperature exceeds a certain threshold.

To implement the thermal management blocks, you should use Verilog code to define the linear equation for converting the temperature sensor output signal into a temperature value. 
You should then use this temperature value to compare to the threshold value and set the alarm signal if necessary. 
Finally, you should use the temperature value and control signals to determine the fan control signal.

module thermal_management (
  input temp_sensor_out,
  input [n-1:0] control,
  output fan_control,
  output alarm
);

parameter n = 4; // number of control signals

// Linear equation to convert temp_sensor_out to temperature value
reg signed [15:0] temperature_value;
always @(*) begin
  temperature_value = (temp_sensor_out * 100) - 2731;
end

// Threshold value based on control signals
reg signed [15:0] threshold_value;
always @(*) begin
  case (control)
    4'b0000: threshold_value = 2500; // Default threshold value
    4'b0001: threshold_value = 3000; // Increase threshold value by 5 degrees Celsius
    4'b0010: threshold_value = 3500; // Increase threshold value by 10 degrees Celsius
    4'b0100: threshold_value = 4000; // Increase threshold value by 15 degrees Celsius
    4'b1000: threshold_value = 4500; // Increase threshold value by 20 degrees Celsius
    default: threshold_value = 2500; // Default threshold value
  endcase
end

// Set alarm signal if temperature exceeds threshold
reg alarm_signal;
always @(temperature_value, threshold_value) begin
  if (temperature_value > threshold_value) begin
    alarm_signal = 1'b1;
  end else begin
    alarm_signal = 1'b0;
  end
end

// Set fan control signal based on temperature value and control signals
reg signed [15:0] fan_control_value;
always @(temperature_value, control) begin
  case (control)
    4'b0000: fan_control_value = 0; // Default fan speed
    4'b0001: fan_control_value = 1000; // Increase fan speed by 10%
    4'b0010: fan_control_value = 2000; // Increase fan speed by 20%
    4'b0100: fan_control_value = 3000; // Increase fan speed by 30%
    4'b1000: fan_control_value = 4000; // Increase fan speed by 40%
    default: fan_control_value = 0; // Default fan speed
  endcase
  
  if (temperature_value > threshold_value) begin
    fan_control_value = fan_control_value * 2; // Double fan speed if temperature exceeds threshold
  end
  
end

assign fan_control = fan_control_value;
assign alarm = alarm_signal;

endmodule

You are tasked with designing a verilog module for a dual-port RAM with the following specifications:
- The module should have two write ports (port A and port B) and two read ports (also port A and port B).
- The memory depth should be configurable using the parameter `MEMD`.
- The data width should be configurable using the parameter `DATAW`.
- The module should be able to initialize the memory with zeros or with a hex file, depending on the value of the parameter `IZERO` and `IFILE`.
- The module should have the following ports:
  - `clk`: the clock signal.
  - `wEnbA`: write enable for port A.
  - `wEnbB`: write enable for port B.
  - `addrA`: write address for port A.
  - `addrB`: write address for port B.
  - `wDataA`: write data for port A.
  - `wDataB`: write data for port B.
  - `rDataA`: read data for port A.
  - `rDataB`: read data for port B.

You are required to implement the `tdpram` module using Verilog.

module tdpram
 #( parameter MEMD  = 2*1024, // memory depth
    parameter DATAW = 16    , // data width
    parameter IZERO = 0     , // binary / Initial RAM with zeros (has priority over IFILE)
    parameter IFILE = ""    ) // initialization hex file (don't pass extension), optional
  ( input                    clk   ,  // clock
    input                    wEnbA ,  // write enable for port A
    input                    wEnbB ,  // write enable for port B
    input  [`log2(MEMD)-1:0] addrA ,  // write addresses - packed from nWPORTS write ports
    input  [`log2(MEMD)-1:0] addrB ,  // write addresses - packed from nWPORTS write ports
    input  [DATAW      -1:0] wDataA,  // write data      - packed from nRPORTS read ports
    input  [DATAW      -1:0] wDataB,  // write data      - packed from nRPORTS read ports
    output reg [DATAW  -1:0] rDataA,  // read  data      - packed from nRPORTS read ports
    output reg [DATAW  -1:0] rDataB); // read  data      - packed from nRPORTS read ports

  // initialize RAM, with zeros if IZERO or file if IFLE.
  integer i;
  reg [DATAW-1:0] mem [0:MEMD-1]; // memory array
  initial
    if (IZERO)
      for (i=0; i<MEMD; i=i+1) mem[i] = {DATAW{1'b0}};
    else
      if (IFILE != "") $readmemh({IFILE,".hex"}, mem);

  // PORT A
  always @(posedge clk) begin
    // write/read; nonblocking statement to read old data
    if (wEnbA) begin
      mem[addrA] <= wDataA; // Change into blocking statement (=) to read new data
      rDataA     <= mem[addrA]; // flow-through
    end else
      rDataA <= mem[addrA]; //Change into blocking statement (=) to read new data
  end

  // PORT B
  always @(posedge clk) begin
    // write/read; nonblocking statement to read old data
    if (wEnbB) begin
      mem[addrB] <= wDataB; // Change into blocking statement (=) to read new data
      rDataB     <= mem[addrB]; // flow-through
    end else
      rDataB <= mem[addrB]; //Change into blocking statement (=) to read new data
  end

endmodule

    input [7:0] b,
    input [1:0] opcode,
    output reg [7:0] result
);

module d_ff_set_clr (
    input CLK,
    input D,
    input SET,
    input CLR,

);

    input clk,
    input rst,
    output reg [3:0] count
);

- `CPOL`: Clock Polarity, a binary value that determines the idle state of the SCK signal. If `CPOL` is 0, the idle state is low. If `CPOL` is 1, the idle state is high.
- `CPHA`: Clock Phase, a binary value that determines the timing of the data transfer. If `CPHA` is 0, data is sampled on the leading edge of SCK and shifted on the trailing edge. If `CPHA` is 1, data is shifted on the leading edge of SCK and sampled on the trailing edge.

The module should have the following ports:

- `i_period`: the input period of the clock signal used to generate the SCK signal.
- `i_xfer`: the input transfer signal used to initiate data transfer.
- `o_sck`: the output SCK signal generated by the module.

The module should generate the SCK signal based on the following truth table:

| CPOL | CPHA | SCK  |
|------|------|------|
| 0    | 0    | i_period & i_xfer |
| 0    | 1    | ~i_period & i_xfer |
| 1    | 0    | ~i_period \| ~i_xfer |
| 1    | 1    | i_period \| ~i_xfer |

Write a Verilog module that implements the `spi_master_sck_gen` module as described above. Your module should be completely self-contained and should be solvable by only one module within 200 lines of Verilog code.

module spi_master_sck_gen
  #(parameter CPOL = 0,
    parameter CPHA = 0)
  (input wire i_period,
   input wire i_xfer,
   output wire o_sck);

  localparam mode = {CPOL[0], CPHA[0]};

  assign o_sck = (mode == 0) ? (i_period & i_xfer) :
                 (mode == 1) ? (~i_period & i_xfer) :
                 (mode == 2) ? (~i_period | ~i_xfer) :
                               (i_period | ~i_xfer);

endmodule

- If in1 is 1, out should be the bitwise OR of in4 and in5, shifted left by 1 bit

- If in6 is less than in7, out should be the bitwise AND of in8 and in9, shifted right by 1 bit

    input in1,
    input [1:0] in2,
    input [2:0] in3,
    input [3:0] in4,
    input [4:0] in5,
    input [5:0] in6,
    input [6:0] in7,
    input [7:0] in8,
    input [8:0] in9,
    output reg [9:0] out
);

        if (in1 == 1'b0) begin
            out = {1'b0, in2 + in3};

            out = out ^ {1'b0, in8, in9};
        end
        else begin
            out = {1'b0, (in8 & in9) >> 1};
        end
    end

endmodule

The module should have two inputs (input_matrix and kernel_matrix) and one output (output_matrix). The input_matrix is a 5x5 matrix represented as a 25-bit vector, and the kernel_matrix is a 3x3 matrix represented as a 9-bit vector. The output_matrix should be a 5x5 matrix represented as a 25-bit vector. Use nested for loops to implement the convolution operation.

module convolution_3x3 (
    input [24:0] input_matrix,
    input [8:0] kernel_matrix,
    output reg [24:0] output_matrix
);

reg [2:0] i, j;
reg [24:0] temp_matrix;

always @(*) begin
    for (i = 0; i < 5; i = i + 1) begin
        for (j = 0; j < 5; j = j + 1) begin
            if (i == 0 || i == 4 || j == 0 || j == 4) begin
                temp_matrix[i*5+j] = 0;
            end else begin
                temp_matrix[i*5+j] = input_matrix[(i-1)*5+(j-1)]*kernel_matrix[0] +
                                     input_matrix[(i-1)*5+j]*kernel_matrix[1] +
                                     input_matrix[(i-1)*5+(j+1)]*kernel_matrix[2] +
                                     input_matrix[i*5+(j-1)]*kernel_matrix[3] +
                                     input_matrix[i*5+j]*kernel_matrix[4] +
                                     input_matrix[i*5+(j+1)]*kernel_matrix[5] +
                                     input_matrix[(i+1)*5+(j-1)]*kernel_matrix[6] +
                                     input_matrix[(i+1)*5+j]*kernel_matrix[7] +
                                     input_matrix[(i+1)*5+(j+1)]*kernel_matrix[8];
            end
        end
    end
end

assign output_matrix = temp_matrix;

endmodule

module divide_by_two (
  input [3:0] in,
  output [2:0] out
);

);

    input reset, // synchronous reset input
    input enable, // counting enable input

);

    if(reset) begin

        if(count == 4'b1001) begin

module adder_4bit (
    input [3:0] a,
    input [3:0] b,
    output reg [4:0] c,
    output reg co
);

always @(*) begin
    {co, c} = a + b;
end

endmodule

module shift_register (
    input clk,
    input [3:0] data_in,
    input load,
    input clear,
    output reg [3:0] data_out
);

always @(posedge clk) begin
    if (clear) begin
        data_out <= 4'b0000;
    end else if (load) begin
        data_out <= data_in;
    end else begin
        data_out <= {data_out[2:0], data_out[3]};
    end
end

endmodule

module control_logic (
    input select,
    input [4:0] adder_out,
    input [3:0] shift_reg_out,
    output reg [4:0] final_out
);

always @(*) begin
    if (select) begin
        final_out = {shift_reg_out, adder_out[4]};
    end else begin
        final_out = shift_reg_out;
    end
end

endmodule

module top_module (
    input clk,
    input reset, // Synchronous active-high reset
    input [3:0] a, // 4-bit input for the adder
    input [3:0] b, // 4-bit input for the adder
    input load, // Parallel load input for the shift register
    input clear, // Synchronous clear input for the shift register
    input select, // Select input to choose between adder and shift register
    output reg [4:0] c, // 5-bit output from the adder
    output reg co, // Carry-out output from the adder
    output reg [3:0] data_out // 4-bit output from the shift register
);

reg [4:0] adder_out;
reg [3:0] shift_reg_out;

adder_4bit adder_inst (
    .a(a),
    .b(b),
    .c(adder_out),
    .co(co)
);

shift_register shift_reg_inst (
    .clk(clk),
    .data_in(adder_out[3:0]),
    .load(load),
    .clear(clear),
    .data_out(shift_reg_out)
);

control_logic control_inst (
    .select(select),
    .adder_out(adder_out),
    .shift_reg_out(shift_reg_out),
    .final_out(c)
);

endmodule

Response:
module up_down_counter (
    input [2:0] D,
    input UD,
    input LD,
    input CLK,
    output reg [2:0] Q
);

always @(posedge CLK) begin
    if (LD) begin
        Q <= D;
    end else begin
        if (UD) begin
            Q <= Q - 1;
        end else begin
            Q <= Q + 1;
        end
    end
end

endmodule

The system should also have an additional functional module that takes in the outputs of both counters and outputs the sum of the two values. The output of the system should be the output of the functional module. The 4-bit counter should count up to 15 and down to 0, while the 3-bit counter should count up to 7 and down to 0. The load input should be synchronous for both counters.

module top_module (
    input clk,
    input areset,
    input load,
    input up_down,
    input select,
    output reg [4:0] counter4,
    output reg [2:0] counter3,
    output reg [5:0] sum
);

reg [4:0] counter4_next;
reg [2:0] counter3_next;

always @(posedge clk or negedge areset) begin
    if (areset == 0) begin
        counter4 <= 0;
        counter3 <= 0;
    end else begin
        if (load) begin
            if (select) begin
                counter4 <= counter4_next;
            end else begin
                counter3 <= counter3_next;
            end
        end else begin
            if (up_down) begin
                if (select) begin
                    if (counter4 == 15) begin
                        counter4_next <= 0;
                    end else begin
                        counter4_next <= counter4 + 1;
                    end
                end else begin
                    if (counter3 == 7) begin
                        counter3_next <= 0;
                    end else begin
                        counter3_next <= counter3 + 1;
                    end
                end
            end else begin
                if (select) begin
                    if (counter4 == 0) begin
                        counter4_next <= 15;
                    end else begin
                        counter4_next <= counter4 - 1;
                    end
                end else begin
                    if (counter3 == 0) begin
                        counter3_next <= 7;
                    end else begin
                        counter3_next <= counter3 - 1;
                    end
                end
            end
        end
    end
end

always @(counter4 or counter3) begin
    sum = counter4 + counter3;
end

endmodule

- `nreset`: an active low asynchronous reset signal

Outputs:

The module should have the following behavior:
- The module should start detecting the sequence "1010" from the beginning of the data stream whenever the reset signal is released.
- Whenever the current bit input `in` is not part of the sequence "1010", the module should reset its detection and start over.
- Whenever the current bit input `in` is part of the sequence "1010", the module should continue detecting the next bits until the entire sequence has been detected.
- Once the sequence "1010" has been detected, the `detected` output should be high until the reset signal is activated again.

module sequence_detector (
  input clk, // clock
  input in, // input bit
  input nreset, // async active low reset
  output detected // output signal
);

  reg [3:0] state; // state variable to keep track of sequence detection

  always @(posedge clk or negedge nreset) begin
    if (!nreset) begin
      state <= 4'b0; // reset state to initial state
      detected <= 1'b0; // reset output
    end else begin
      case (state)
        4'b0000: if (in == 1'b1) state <= 4'b0001; // detected 1
                 else state <= 4'b0000; // reset
        4'b0001: if (in == 1'b0) state <= 4'b0010; // detected 10
                 else if (in == 1'b1) state <= 4'b0001; // detected 1
                 else state <= 4'b0000; // reset
        4'b0010: if (in == 1'b1) state <= 4'b0011; // detected 101
                 else state <= 4'b0000; // reset
        4'b0011: if (in == 1'b0) state <= 4'b0100; // detected 1010
                 else if (in == 1'b1) state <= 4'b0001; // detected 1
                 else state <= 4'b0000; // reset
        4'b0100: begin // sequence detected
                   detected <= 1'b1; // set output
                   state <= 4'b0100; // stay in state
                 end
      endcase
    end
  end

endmodule

When shift is low, the module should behave like a regular D flip-flop, storing the value of d on the rising edge of clk. When shift is high, the module should shift the stored value to the next flip-flop on the rising edge of clk. The output of the third flip-flop should be the output of the module.

The additional functional module should take in two 4-bit inputs and a select input, which determines whether to perform addition or subtraction. The output should be the result of the selected operation. When select is high, the module should perform addition by passing the inputs through the ripple carry adder module and outputting the sum. When select is low, the module should perform subtraction by inverting the second input and passing both inputs through the ripple carry adder module, then adding 1 to the output.

module ripple_carry_adder (
  input [3:0] in1, // First 4-bit input
  input [3:0] in2, // Second 4-bit input
  output [3:0] sum, // 4-bit sum output
  output carry_out // Carry-out output
);

  wire [3:0] carry; // Internal carry wires

  full_adder fa0(in1[0], in2[0], 1'b0, sum[0], carry[0]); // First full adder with carry-in of 0
  full_adder fa1(in1[1], in2[1], carry[0], sum[1], carry[1]); // Second full adder with carry-in from first full adder
  full_adder fa2(in1[2], in2[2], carry[1], sum[2], carry[2]); // Third full adder with carry-in from second full adder
  full_adder fa3(in1[3], in2[3], carry[2], sum[3], carry_out); // Fourth full adder with carry-in from third full adder and carry-out as output

endmodule

module full_adder (
  input a, // First input bit
  input b, // Second input bit
  input carry_in, // Carry-in bit
  output sum, // Sum output bit
  output carry_out // Carry-out output bit
);

  assign {carry_out, sum} = a + b + carry_in; // Sum and carry-out calculation using concatenation and addition operator

endmodule

module shift_register (
  input clk, // Clock input
  input d, // Data input
  input shift, // Shift input to determine shift or store mode
  output reg [2:0] q // Output of the third flip-flop
);

  always @(posedge clk) begin
    if (shift) begin // Shift mode
      q <= {q[1:0], d}; // Shift stored value to next flip-flop and store new value in first flip-flop
    end else begin // Store mode
      q <= d; // Store value in first flip-flop
    end
  end

endmodule

module functional_module (
  input [3:0] in1, // First 4-bit input
  input [3:0] in2, // Second 4-bit input
  input select, // Select input to choose between addition and subtraction
  output [3:0] out // 4-bit output of selected operation
);

  wire [3:0] adder_out; // Output of ripple carry adder module
  wire [3:0] inv_in2; // Inverted second input for subtraction
  wire carry_out; // Carry-out from ripple carry adder module

  ripple_carry_adder rca(in1, inv_in2, adder_out, carry_out); // Ripple carry adder module instantiation
  assign inv_in2 = ~in2 + 1; // Invert second input and add 1 for two's complement representation in subtraction

  always @(*) begin
    if (select) begin // Addition mode
      out = adder_out; // Output sum from ripple carry adder module
    end else begin // Subtraction mode
      out = adder_out + 1; // Add 1 to output of ripple carry adder module for two's complement representation in subtraction
    end
  end

endmodule

module control_logic (
  input select, // Select input to choose between shift register and functional module
  input [3:0] in1, // First 4-bit input
  input [3:0] in2, // Second 4-bit input
  input clk, // Clock input for shift register module
  input reset, // Synchronous active-high reset for shift register module
  output [3:0] out // Output of active module
);

  wire [2:0] shift_reg_out; // Output of shift register module
  wire [3:0] func_mod_out; // Output of functional module

  shift_register sr(clk, in1[0], select, shift_reg_out[0]); // Shift register module instantiation
  functional_module fm(in1, in2, select, func_mod_out); // Functional module instantiation

  always @(*) begin
    if (select) begin // Functional module active
      out = func_mod_out; // Output of functional module
    end else begin // Shift register module active
      out = {shift_reg_out, in1[3:1]}; // Output of shift register module concatenated with last 3 bits of first input
    end
  end

endmodule

module top_module ( 
  input clk, 
  input reset, // Synchronous active-high reset
  input [3:0] in1, // First 4-bit input
  input [3:0] in2, // Second 4-bit input
  input select, // Select input to choose between shift register and functional module
  output [3:0] out // 4-bit output from the active module
);

  wire [3:0] control_logic_out; // Output of control logic module

  control_logic cl(select, in1, in2, clk, reset, control_logic_out); // Control logic module instantiation

  assign out = control_logic_out; // Output of control logic module

- `clk` (1-bit): clock input
- `reset` (1-bit): asynchronous reset input (active low)
- `ce` (1-bit): clock enable input (active high)
- `d` (1-bit): data input

Outputs:
- `q` (1-bit): data output
- `notifier` (1-bit): output that goes high for one clock cycle when the flip-flop output changes

The flip-flop should behave as follows:
- When `reset` is asserted, `q` should be set to 0 and `notifier` should be set to 1 for one clock cycle.
- When `ce` is deasserted, the flip-flop should hold its current state.
- When `ce` is asserted, the flip-flop should update its output on the rising edge of the clock, according to the input `d`.
- When the output `q` changes, `notifier` should be set to 1 for one clock cycle.

You should write a Verilog module that implements the above behavior. Your implementation should be contained within a single module and should not exceed 200 lines of code.

module dff_reset_ce_notifier(
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input ce,
    input d,
    output reg q,
    output reg notifier
);

reg q_next;

always @(posedge clk or negedge reset)
begin
    if (!reset) begin
        q <= 1'b0;
        notifier <= 1'b1;
    end
    else if (ce) begin
        q_next <= d;
        notifier <= (q_next != q);
    end
end

always @(posedge clk)
begin
    if (ce) begin
        q <= q_next;
    end
end

endmodule

- `SCD` (input): a single-bit scan chain data signal
- `SCE` (input): a single-bit scan chain enable signal

- `VPWR` (input): a power supply voltage signal
- `VGND` (input): a ground voltage signal
- `VPB` (input): a power supply voltage signal for the scan chain
- `VNB` (input): a ground voltage signal for the scan chain

- When `RESET_B` is high, `Q` should follow the value of `D` on each rising edge of `CLK`.
- When `SCE` is high, the module should enter scan mode and `Q` should follow the value of `SCD` on each rising edge of `CLK`.
- When `SCE` is low, the module should exit scan mode and resume normal operation.

module sky130_fd_sc_hd__sdfrtp (
    output Q,
    input CLK,
    input D,
    input SCD,
    input SCE,
    input RESET_B,
    input VPWR,
    input VGND,
    input VPB,
    input VNB
);

        if (!RESET_B) begin
            Q_reg <= 1'b0;
        end else if (SCE) begin
            Q_reg <= SCD;
        end else begin
            Q_reg <= D;
        end
    end

endmodule
